import numpy as np
import pandas as pd


def _to_vec(x):
    """Robustly convert a cell (list/tuple/ndarray/str) to a float 1-D array."""
    if isinstance(x, np.ndarray):
        return x.astype(float)
    if isinstance(x, (list, tuple)):
        return np.asarray(list(x), dtype=float)
    s = str(x).strip().replace("[", " ").replace("]", " ").replace(",", " ")
    return np.asarray(s.split(), dtype=float)


def metric(data: pd.DataFrame) -> float:
    df = data.reset_index(drop=True)
    n_rows = len(df)
    if n_rows == 0:
        return 0.0

    A = np.vstack([_to_vec(x) for x in df["option_a_ratings"]])
    B = np.vstack([_to_vec(x) for x in df["option_b_ratings"]])
    n_feat = A.shape[1]

    # Design validities [0.95, 0.85, 0.75, 0.65, 0.60]; fall back gracefully.
    v = np.array([0.95, 0.85, 0.75, 0.65, 0.60], dtype=float)
    if v.shape[0] != n_feat:
        v = np.linspace(0.95, 0.60, n_feat)

    # Chose-A indicator (response: 0 = A, 1 = B).
    y = (np.asarray(df["response"], dtype=float) == 0.0).astype(float)

    a_win = A > B
    b_win = B > A

    # Signed tally margin (Tallying's ONLY explanatory variable).
    margin = a_win.sum(axis=1).astype(float) - b_win.sum(axis=1).astype(float)

    # Validity-weighted evidence difference (NVW's driving quantity).
    d = (a_win * v).sum(axis=1) - (b_win * v).sum(axis=1)

    # OLS: y ~ 1 + margin + d. Return the partial coefficient on d.
    X = np.column_stack([np.ones(n_rows), margin, d])
    beta, _, _, _ = np.linalg.lstsq(X, y, rcond=None)
    return float(beta[2])
metric.rationale:
The metric is the partial OLS coefficient of the validity-weighted evidence difference d = sum(v over A-won cues) - sum(v over B-won cues) in a regression of the chose-A indicator on [intercept, signed tally margin, d], pooled over all trials.

WHY IT IS EXACTLY ZERO UNDER TALLYING (for every beta, epsilon): Tallying's P(A) = sigmoid(beta*(a_wins - b_wins)) (plus a symmetric lapse), i.e., a function of the signed margin m alone. The design's trial set is perfectly mirrored within every margin level: the d-values of all trials sharing a given margin sum to exactly zero (margin 0: +0.55,+0.40,+0.15,0,+0.05,-0.55,-0.40,-0.15,0,-0.05; margin +1: +1.30...+0.20 with the exact negatives in margin -1; margin +2: +1.90,+1.05 with exact negatives). Hence E[d | m] = 0 for each m, so the residual of d after projecting on m is orthogonal to any function of m, including Tallying's (possibly nonlinear) mean choice function. The d-coefficient is therefore exactly zero in expectation under Tallying, for ALL of its parameter values, with only binomial sampling noise around zero.

WHY IT IS ROBUSTLY POSITIVE UNDER NVW (for every admissible parameter): NVW's P(A) is monotone increasing in the validity-weighted evidence difference (v^gamma preserves validity order for gamma in [0.7,1.3], so the sign and rank of d computed with raw v is preserved), and the design provides large within-margin spread of d (margin 0: |d| up to 0.55; margin 1: 0.20 to 1.30; margin 2: 1.05 to 1.90). The within-margin d-slope of the logistic is approximately beta_eff * p(1-p) with beta_eff = beta*delta in [0.9, 3.3], so even at the worst-case corner (beta=5, delta=0.18) the slope is >= ~0.19, and at mid parameters (~2.1) it is ~0.4-0.5. The one-reason lapse component (top-cue direction) is itself aligned with sign(d) on the high-|d| trials and only adds to the slope. The lapse epsilon (<=0.06) shrinks the slope by at most 6%.

POWER AT N=25: The pooled within-margin residual variance of d is ~0.70 and each subject contributes 96 trials, so the per-subject standard error of the d-coefficient is about sqrt(0.25/(96*0.70)) ~ 0.06 (worst case, Tallying with low beta; NVW's is smaller because its p(1-p) is smaller at extreme d). Welch's t for a mean gap of even 0.19 (absolute worst-case NVW corner) vs 0 (Tallying) is then roughly 0.19 / sqrt((0.0037+0.0022)/25) ~ 12-14, far below alpha=0.01; at typical parameters the gap (~0.4-0.5) gives t > 25. The metric works identically on the pooled DataFrame and on a single subject's 96-trial slice (the regression is well-conditioned in both cases), so the between-subject variance is well defined. The contrast is structural (Tallying literally has no within-margin sensitivity; NVW does), not a parameter tuning, and cannot be trivially satisfied by the advocated theory's noise terms.

proposer_theory.description: Noisy Validity-weighted evidence integration with capacity-interference and one-reason lapses (NVW). People do not use a single fixed heuristic; they pool all the expert ratings they can, but each cue's contribution is weighted by its validity raised to a steepness exponent gamma (gamma = 0 recovers Tallying, gamma -> infinity recovers Take-The-Best, so both classic heuristics are limiting cases). Integration is capacity-limited: beyond a working-memory span of about four cues, every additional cue that must be pooled multiplies the reliability (effective inverse temperature) of the integrated comparison by an interference factor delta < 1, so choice consistency is design-dependent and falls sharply as feature count grows. Each cue is additionally attended only with probability alpha (lapses of attention). On a minority of trials — with a probability omega that is modulated by how strongly the most valid discriminating cue's validity dominates the validity of the opposing side's cues — the agent abandons integration and makes a one-reason decision based solely on that top cue. The final choice is a softmax (at the capacity-scaled inverse temperature) over the attended, validity-weighted evidence difference, mixed with an independent lapse to uniform guessing.
proposer_theory.predict_source:
def predict(parameters, state, history):
    # NVW: Noisy Validity-weighted integration with capacity-interference
    # and one-reason lapses.
    # Stimulus: array of shape (2, n_features); row 0 = option A, row 1 = B.
    stim = np.asarray(state, dtype=float)
    if stim.ndim != 2 or stim.shape[0] != 2:
        raise ValueError(
            f"NVW expects a (2, n_features) stimulus; got shape {stim.shape}."
        )
    a, b = stim[0], stim[1]
    n = int(stim.shape[1])

    v = np.asarray(parameters["validities"], dtype=float).ravel()
    if v.shape[0] != n:
        raise ValueError(
            f"validities length {v.shape[0]} != n_features {n}."
        )

    gamma = float(parameters["gamma"])
    alpha = float(parameters["alpha"])
    beta = float(parameters["beta"])
    delta = float(parameters["delta"])
    epsilon = float(parameters["epsilon"])
    omega_base = float(parameters["omega_base"])
    omega_dom = float(parameters["omega_dom"])

    # (1) Validity-steepness weights: gamma = 0 -> Tallying (equal weights),
    # gamma -> infinity -> Take-The-Best (top cue only).
    w = np.power(v, gamma)

    # (3) Attention: each cue independently attended with probability alpha.
    att = np.random.random(n) < alpha
    a_win = (a > b) & att
    b_win = (b > a) & att
    disc = a_win | b_win

    # (3) Capacity / interference: beyond a working-memory span of ~4 cues,
    # each additional cue that must be pooled multiplies the reliability
    # (effective inverse temperature) of the integrated evidence by delta.
    # This makes decision noise grow with feature count.
    excess = max(0, n - 4)
    beta_eff = beta * (delta ** excess)

    def _sig(z):
        # Numerically stable logistic.
        return 0.5 * (1.0 + np.tanh(0.5 * np.asarray(z, dtype=float)))

    if not np.any(disc):
        # No attended discriminating cue: pure guess.
        p_a = 0.5
    else:
        # (1) Integration: softmax over the weighted evidence difference.
        d = float(np.sum(w[a_win]) - np.sum(w[b_win]))
        p_int = float(_sig(beta_eff * d))

        # (2) One-reason mode: the single most valid attended
        # discriminating cue decides (TTB-like), with confidence scaled
        # by that cue's weight and the effective sensitivity.
        idx = np.where(disc)[0]
        top = int(idx[np.argmax(v[idx])])
        s = 1.0 if a[top] > b[top] else -1.0
        p_1r = float(_sig(beta_eff * w[top] * s))

        # (2) Validity-dominance coupling for the one-reason lapse rate:
        # dominance of the top cue over the opposing side's cue validities.
        opp = b_win if s > 0 else a_win
        if np.any(opp):
            dom = float(v[top] - np.mean(v[opp]))
        else:
            dom = float(v[top] - 0.5)
        omega_t = float(np.clip(omega_base + omega_dom * dom, 0.0, 0.95))

        p_a = (1.0 - omega_t) * p_int + omega_t * p_1r

    probs = np.array([p_a, 1.0 - p_a], dtype=float)

    # (4) Independent lapse toward uniform guessing.
    probs = (1.0 - epsilon) * probs + epsilon * 0.5
    return probs
proposer_theory.rationale:
DIAGNOSIS OF PRIOR FAILURES. TTB (pi_1) predicts P(choose TTB winner | conflict) = 0.84 in Experiment 1 (real: 0.208) and a strongly negative tally-minus-TTB contrast of -0.48 in Experiment 2 (real: +0.158): it is far too one-reason driven. Tallying (pi_2) is almost right in Experiment 1 (0.136 vs 0.208, i.e. tally-consistency 0.86 vs real 0.79) but predicts the SAME invariant consistency in Experiment 2 (0.548 vs real 0.158, i.e. tally-consistency 0.86 vs real 0.605). The signature of the human data is therefore: (i) mostly integration, mildly validity-sensitive (slightly more TTB-leaning than pure tallying in Exp 1), and (ii) a large DROP in integration consistency when the cue set grows from 5 to 6 features. Crucially, I verified analytically that the two designs are matched on every conflict-trial statistic that a fixed-noise integrator sees (weighted margins, SNR, dominance of the top cue — if anything top-cue dominance is HIGHER in Exp 1), so no shared-parameter validity weighting alone can produce the gap; the gap must be carried by a feature-count-dependent noise term. This is exactly the arbiter's mechanism (3): 'effective decision noise grows with feature count'.

MECHANISMS. NVW implements the arbiter's prescription: (1) weights w_j = v_j^gamma nest Tallying (gamma=0) and TTB (gamma->inf); (2) a one-reason lapse mode with rate omega coupled to the validity dominance of the top discriminating cue over the opposing majority's cues; (3) cue-wise attention alpha plus a capacity/interference term: beyond a working-memory span of ~4 cues, each extra pooled cue multiplies evidence reliability by delta, so noise grows steeply with feature count; (4) softmax response rule with inverse temperature beta plus an independent lapse epsilon.

CALIBRATION LOGIC. Because parameters are sampled per subject from the declared ranges and metrics are computed on the pooled population, the ranges themselves are the population-level fit (this is visible in pi_2: its 0.86 tally-consistency in BOTH experiments equals 1 - E[epsilon]/2 under uniform sampling of epsilon in [0, 0.5]). I therefore derived the ranges analytically from the conflict-trial structure of both designs so that the SAME parameter distribution reproduces both targets: with gamma ~ U[0.7, 1.3], beta ~ U[5, 11], delta ~ U[0.18, 0.30], the effective Exp-1 sensitivity is beta*delta (mean ~1.9) and the effective Exp-2 sensitivity is beta*delta^2 (mean ~0.47). Averaging the logistic over these ranges yields Exp-1 tally-consistency ~0.79-0.80 (metric P(TTB winner|conflict) ~ 0.20-0.22, real 0.208) and Exp-2 tally-consistency ~0.60-0.61 (metric ~0.15-0.17, real 0.158). The one-reason lapse (omega ~ 0.02) and lapse (epsilon ~ 0.03) contribute the small residual top-cue choices without materially shifting the averages. This is why I propose tighter ranges than the arbiter's illustrative ones: under per-subject uniform sampling, wide ranges (e.g. gamma in [0,4]) would average TTB-like and tally-like subjects and destroy the fit; the ranges above are centered on the region that both experiments jointly identify.

DEVIATION FROM ARBITER DETAIL. I keep the validity-dominance coupling for omega but let its slope (omega_dom) be free-signed: computing actual dominance values (top-cue validity minus mean opposing validity) gives a HIGHER mean in Exp 1 (0.23) than Exp 2 (0.19), so an increasing-with-dominance coupling would push Experiment 1 toward TTB — the opposite of what the data show. The between-experiment gap is instead carried by the capacity-interference term, which is the arbiter's own mechanism (3). The coupling remains in the model, falsifiable against new designs that manipulate the validity gap at fixed tally margins.

FALSIFIABLE PREDICTIONS. NVW predicts (a) choice consistency falls sharply (geometrically) as feature count grows beyond ~4 at fixed tally margins — distinguishing it from Tallying's invariance; (b) deviations from tally invariance that grow with the validity spread of the cues (via gamma); (c) a small, validity-dominance-modulated minority of pure one-reason choices. It can be validated on new designs that independently manipulate feature count and the top-cue validity gap.

experiment.rationale: This design attacks NVW's central and most falsifiable structural claim: capacity interference. NVW asserts that beyond a working-memory span of ~4 cues, each additional pooled cue multiplies the effective inverse temperature by delta < 1, so choice consistency collapses as feature count grows. Tallying has no capacity limit: its softmax inverse temperature beta is design-independent, and its predicted probability depends only on win counts. I therefore set n_features = 8 (four cues beyond the span), which drives NVW's effective sensitivity to beta_eff = beta * delta^4 <= 11 * 0.30^4 = 0.089. Since the maximum possible validity-weighted evidence difference across all trials is |d| <= sum(v^gamma) <= 6.34 (at gamma = 0.7), NVW's predicted P(A) is HARD-BOUNDED to roughly [0.37, 0.64] on every single trial, for every admissible parameter setting (the one-reason lapse uses the same tiny beta_eff, and epsilon/omega only shrink deviations further; attention lapses at alpha <= 1 compress it even more). Tallying, in contrast, predicts a steep, margin-graded ladder: sigmoid(beta), sigmoid(2*beta), sigmoid(4*beta), sigmoid(6*beta) across the margin gradient G1->G4, and near-deterministic choice on the anchor trials E1/E2 (e.g., sigmoid(8*beta) >= 0.98 for beta >= 0.5). The design thus yields three decisive, parameter-free signatures: (1) CAPACITY CLIFF: observed choice proportions on unambiguous anchors (E1: 8-0 split; E2: 7-1 split) exceeding ~0.7 are impossible for NVW at ANY admissible parameter combination, while trivially accommodated by Tallying; likewise, a spread across the margin ladder (G1 vs G4) exceeding ~0.12 is impossible for NVW (its maximum ladder spread is sigmoid(0.089*4.73) - sigmoid(0.089*0.98) ~ 0.08) but natural for Tallying. (2) FIXED-COUNT VALIDITY GRADIENT: trials S1, S2, S3 all have identical win counts (4,3) but validity-weighted evidence d = +1.63, +0.99, -0.37 (order preserved for all gamma in [0.7, 1.3], verified at both endpoints, since v^gamma preserves validity order). Tallying predicts EXACTLY identical probabilities on all three; NVW predicts a strictly decreasing series with S3 below 0.5. Similarly, the tie trials Z1 (d = +1.11), Z2 (d = +0.25), Z3 (d = -0.19) all have counts (4,4): Tallying predicts exactly 0.5 on all three; NVW predicts a strictly ordered series crossing 0.5 between Z2 and Z3. (3) MATCHED-COUNT ALLEGIANCE: G4 and E2 both have counts (7,1) — Tallying predicts identical probabilities; NVW predicts P(G4) > P(E2) strictly, because both the integrated evidence (d = 4.73 vs 3.81) and the one-reason component (top cue favors the tally winner in G4, opposes it in E2) align. Conversely, if NVW is correct, subjects should be near-chance everywhere with only a small d-ordered ripple — a profile Tallying can only mimic by taking beta near 0, which would then destroy the margin ladder Tallying needs elsewhere; the joint pattern (near-chance + d-ordering at fixed counts) is uniquely NVW, while (steep ladder + exact flatness at fixed counts) is uniquely Tallying. Every trial type appears in A/B-mirrored pairs to absorb side and position bias. With 24 unique pairs, K = 96 // 24 = 4, giving exactly 96 trials per subject.

metric.metric_source:
def metric(data: pd.DataFrame) -> float:
    """Anchor-allegiance: proportion of trials with a large tally margin
    (|a_wins - b_wins| >= 6) on which the subject chose the option that
    wins on more features (the tally winner).

    Under Tallying, these are the unambiguous anchors (8-0 and 7-1 splits:
    design trials 7, 8, 21, 22, 23, 24 and their 4 repetitions = 24 trials
    per subject), where the softmax over tallies predicts near-deterministic
    choice for any non-trivial beta. Under NVW, the capacity-interference
    factor delta^4 crushes the effective inverse temperature to
    beta_eff <= 11 * 0.30^4 ~ 0.09, so even the maximum validity-weighted
    evidence difference (~6) yields P ~ sigmoid(0.5) <= 0.64; attention
    lapses and the uniform-mixing epsilon only pull this further toward
    0.5. The two theories therefore make sharply separated predictions on
    this proportion, and the A/B-mirrored anchors cancel side bias.
    """
    a_col = data['option_a_ratings']
    b_col = data['option_b_ratings']
    r_col = data['response']

    n_anchor = 0
    n_hit = 0

    for ra, rb, resp in zip(a_col, b_col, r_col):
        va = np.asarray(ra, dtype=float)
        vb = np.asarray(rb, dtype=float)
        if va.shape != vb.shape:
            continue

        a_wins = float(np.sum(va > vb))
        b_wins = float(np.sum(vb > va))
        margin = a_wins - b_wins

        if abs(margin) >= 6:
            n_anchor += 1
            winner_is_a = margin > 0
            chose_a = (int(resp) == 0)
            if chose_a == winner_is_a:
                n_hit += 1

    if n_anchor == 0:
        return 0.5
    return float(n_hit) / float(n_anchor)
metric.rationale: The metric isolates the design's single strongest parameter-free signature: the capacity cliff on unambiguous anchors. Trials 7/8 (7-1 split), 21/22 (8-0 split) and 23/24 (7-1 split) all have tally margins of 6 or 8, giving 6 unique pairs x 4 reps = 24 anchor trials per subject, so the per-subject estimate is based on a decent sample and its between-subject variance is just binomial noise. Tallying predicts P(choose tally winner) = sigmoid(beta*margin)*(1-eps) + eps/2, which is >= ~0.95 for any moderately fitted beta (and still ~0.6 even at the extreme low end beta=0.1, eps=0.5). NVW is hard-bounded: with n_features=8 the capacity interference forces beta_eff = beta*delta^4 <= 11*0.30^4 ~ 0.089, so even the largest possible validity-weighted evidence difference (sum of v^gamma ~ 6.3) gives P <= sigmoid(0.56) ~ 0.64, and the one-reason lapse, attention lapses (alpha < 1 shrink d), and uniform-mixing epsilon all compress this toward 0.5. No admissible NVW parameter combination can push anchor allegiance above ~0.64, while Tallying naturally sits near 1. The A/B mirroring of every anchor pair absorbs side/position bias, so the proportion is a clean readout of margin-driven (count-based) choice rather than response bias. Expected separation: ~0.95+ (self) vs ~0.55-0.60 (adv), with per-subject standard deviations of ~0.05 and ~0.10 respectively, yielding a Welch t-statistic well above 10 at N=25 and p far below 0.01.

proposer_theory.description: People compare two options by counting, across all features, how often one option has a higher value than the other. The option that wins on more features is chosen. Tallying discards cardinal magnitudes — only the sign of each feature-wise comparison matters — so the heuristic is robust to monotone rescaling of individual features and cannot be swayed by a single large feature difference in the way Equal-Weight can. Ties on an individual feature contribute nothing to either count: that cue is simply treated as uninformative for the pair. No feature is privileged, in contrast to Take The Best; every cue contributes equally to the tally. When the two counts are equal the heuristic has no basis for preference and the learner must guess. Response noise enters through a softmax over the two tallies with inverse temperature beta (interpolating between fully deterministic choice at large beta and uniform guessing at beta = 0), plus an independent lapse that with probability epsilon replaces the softmax output with a uniform pick over the two options.
proposer_theory.predict_source:
def predict(parameters, stimulus, history):
    # Paper-faithful Tallying heuristic (Dawes 1979; Gigerenzer &
    # Goldstein 1999). Stimulus is the pair of option feature vectors
    # for the current trial: array-like of shape (2, n_features),
    # with row 0 = option A, row 1 = option B. History is ignored.
    stim = np.asarray(stimulus, dtype=float)
    if stim.ndim != 2 or stim.shape[0] != 2:
        raise ValueError(
            f"Tallying expects a (2, n_features) stimulus; got shape {stim.shape}."
        )

    a, b = stim[0], stim[1]
    # Count strict feature-wise wins; ties contribute to neither option.
    a_wins = float(np.sum(a > b))
    b_wins = float(np.sum(b > a))
    scores = np.array([a_wins, b_wins])

    beta = float(parameters["beta"])
    epsilon = float(parameters["epsilon"])

    # Softmax with max-subtraction for numerical stability. When
    # a_wins == b_wins the softmax is exactly uniform regardless of
    # beta, which is the correct behavior for an undiscriminating
    # tally.
    z = beta * (scores - scores.max())
    e = np.exp(z)
    p_core = e / e.sum()

    n_opts = p_core.shape[0]
    return (1.0 - epsilon) * p_core + epsilon * (np.ones(n_opts) / n_opts)

next_theory.description: Subjective-Weighted Counting with convex cue-order recency (SWC), deterministic-attention variant. People integrate ALL discriminating cues additively with no capacity interference, but the cue weights are subjective and only partially calibrated to communicated validities: w_j = (1-lambda)/n + lambda*[(1-rho)*vnorm_j + rho*(j/(n-1))^eta]. Because validities are always presented in strictly decreasing feature order, the convex recency gradient is anti-correlated with validity, producing within-margin anti-validity preferences (Experiment 3's negative d-coefficient) while preserving mostly-tally aggregate behavior. Attention to cues is deterministic (every cue is always attended); the only stochasticity is the logistic choice noise itself plus a small uniform lapse epsilon. This edition implements the critic's in-family tuning: the noise channels that let the fit collapse to flat counting are removed or tightened so the recency gradient must do the work.
next_theory.predict_source:
def predict(parameters, state, history):
    # SWC: Subjective-Weighted Counting with convex cue-order recency
    # (deterministic-attention variant).
    # Stimulus: array of shape (2, n_features); row 0 = option A, row 1 = B.
    stim = np.asarray(state, dtype=float)
    if stim.ndim != 2 or stim.shape[0] != 2:
        raise ValueError(
            f"SWC expects a (2, n_features) stimulus; got shape {stim.shape}."
        )
    a, b = stim[0], stim[1]
    n = int(stim.shape[1])

    v = np.asarray(parameters["validities"], dtype=float).ravel()
    if v.shape[0] != n:
        # Graceful fallback: linearly decreasing validities.
        v = np.linspace(0.95, 0.55, n)

    lam = float(parameters["lambda"])
    rho = float(parameters["rho"])
    eta = float(parameters["eta"])
    beta = float(parameters["beta"])
    eps = float(parameters["epsilon"])

    # (1) Subjective validity component: min-max normalized validities.
    vspan = float(v.max() - v.min())
    if vspan > 1e-12:
        vnorm = (v - v.min()) / vspan
    else:
        vnorm = np.full(n, 0.5)

    # (2) Recency component: position in presentation order, convexly
    # transformed so that late cues can be strongly overweighted.
    if n > 1:
        pos = (np.arange(n, dtype=float) / (n - 1.0)) ** eta
    else:
        pos = np.full(n, 0.5)

    # Subjective weights: mixture of flat counting, validity-following,
    # and recency-following. Because validities are presented in strictly
    # decreasing feature order, the recency part is anti-correlated with
    # validity -- the source of within-margin anti-validity preferences.
    g = (1.0 - rho) * vnorm + rho * pos
    w = (1.0 - lam) / n + lam * g

    # (3) Deterministic attention: every cue is attended on every trial
    # (per-cue attention lapse removed -- real subjects are highly
    # consistent, and stochastic lapses were the dominant noise source
    # inflating between-subject variance).
    s = np.sign(a - b)

    # Additive integration of all discriminating cues.
    # NO capacity interference: beta is design-independent.
    d = float(np.sum(w * s))

    # Numerically stable logistic.
    p_a = 0.5 * (1.0 + np.tanh(0.5 * beta * d))
    probs = np.array([p_a, 1.0 - p_a], dtype=float)

    # (4) Independent uniform lapse.
    probs = (1.0 - eps) * probs + eps * 0.5
    return probs
next_theory.rationale: Minimal-diff edit of the accepted SWC base, applying the critic's four in-family prescriptions. (1) CUT THE NOISE: the per-cue stochastic attention (alpha drawn per trial) was removed entirely — every cue is now always attended. This was the dominant variance source behind Experiment 3's between-subject variance of 0.2046 (real: 0.0186): binomial per-cue dropout made single subjects wildly inconsistent and let the fit soften aggregate rates with noise instead of using the recency gradient. The uniform lapse epsilon is retained but tightened to [0, 0.03]. (2) FORCE THE RECENCY GRADIENT TO ENGAGE: lambda is now [0.8, 1.0], rho [0.8, 1.0], eta [2.5, 4.5], so the flat-counting collapse (lambda ~ 0) that produced Exp 3 ~ 0 is unreachable; the mixture is always dominated by the graded (validity + convex recency) component. (3) MODERATE BETA: beta is capped at 1.7 (previous range went to 8), so conflict probabilities stay in the 0.6-0.9 band rather than saturating — this is what Experiment 2's near-indifferent contrast (real 0.158) requires. (4) ANCHORS: with no interference and moderate beta, hand computation at the range midpoint (lambda~0.9, rho~0.9, eta~3.5, beta~1.2) gives: Exp 4 anchor allegiance ~0.83 (real 0.843) — the 7-1 anchors with the loss on the last cue land near p~0.65, cooling the previous 0.900; Exp 1 TTB-adherence ~0.21 (real 0.208); Exp 2 contrast ~0.19-0.21 (real 0.158, down from 0.321); Exp 3 partial d-coefficient ~ -0.4 at the midpoint and ~ -0.55 to -0.68 at the recency-heavy corner (rho -> 1, lambda -> 1, beta ~1.2-1.3), bracketing the real -0.5756 — a massive improvement over the previous +0.026. The convex recency term is preserved unchanged: it remains the only in-family degree of freedom that yields Experiment 3's negative within-margin coefficient while keeping Experiments 1, 2 and 4 near their targets, and the tightened ranges now force the fit into that basin instead of the noise-dominated flat-counting region the previous parameterization permitted.

experiment.rationale:
STRUCTURAL LEVER. With validities fixed per feature, both theories reduce to a fixed position-indexed weight profile applied to the cue-allegiance pattern s_j = sign(A_j - B_j): NVW uses w_j ∝ v_j^gamma (validity-VALUE based), while SWC uses w_j = (1-lambda)/n + lambda[(1-rho)vnorm_j + rho*(j/(n-1))^eta] (position-RECENCY based, with recency necessarily dominating: lam*rho >= 0.64 versus a validity coefficient <= 0.20 and flat <= 0.20 across SWC's entire box). I therefore present validities in STRICTLY DECREASING order [0.95, 0.90, 0.85, 0.62, 0.56, 0.52] — SWC's own assumed presentation format, i.e., its home turf — with a sharp validity gap between positions 3 and 4 creating a 'high-validity early block' {0.95, 0.90, 0.85} and a 'low-validity late block' {0.62, 0.56, 0.52}. This makes the two weight profiles strongly ANTI-CORRELATED: NVW's weights fall with position, SWC's rise (convexly) with position. n_features = 6 also places two cues beyond NVW's span-4, engaging its capacity-interference signature (beta_eff = beta*delta^2 in [0.16, 0.99], i.e., NVW itself predicts compressed confidence), while SWC's beta is design-independent.

DISSOCIATION AXES (all predicted boxes verified at the corners of BOTH parameter spaces; NVW's d-sign is invariant over gamma in [0.7, 1.3] because v^gamma is monotone in v, and SWC's recency dominance holds over its whole box):

(1) SIGN-FLIP FAMILY (S1, S2, S3, E1, E3, T3, T6, T8 + mirrors; 16 of 24 trials). The early high-validity block favors one option and the late low-validity block the other. NVW predicts the early-block (validity) winner; SWC predicts the late-block (recency) winner — PARAMETER-FREE OPPOSITE SIGNS. Headline boxes for P(A): S1 (A wins only expert 6 vs expert 1): NVW 0.39-0.51, SWC 0.60-0.85. S2 (A wins experts 5-6 vs 1-2): NVW 0.28-0.48, SWC 0.64-0.91. S3 (A wins experts 4-6 vs 1-3): NVW 0.25-0.47, SWC 0.63-0.91. E1 — the most damning trial for SWC: B wins the FOUR MOST VALID experts and A only the two least valid, yet SWC still predicts A (P(A) in [0.55, 0.88]) because recency weight on the last two positions outweighs everything; NVW predicts B (P(A) in [0.10, 0.41]). E3: A wins the two top experts vs B's single bottom expert — SWC predicts B (P(A) in [0.18, 0.41]) because one late cue outweighs two top cues; NVW predicts A (0.55-0.80). T6/T8 extend the flip to mixed patterns (boxes: NVW 0.52-0.71 vs SWC 0.09-0.37; NVW 0.44-0.50 vs SWC 0.62-0.89).

(2) VALIDITY-TIE / RECENCY-ONLY (T1, T1m). A wins experts 1 and 6, B wins experts 3 and 4: the validity-weighted evidence is exactly balanced (|d| <= 0.04 for all gamma), so NVW predicts chance (P(A) in [0.50, 0.55], the tiny upward tilt being its one-reason lapse toward the top cue), while SWC's recency gradient (expert 6 vs experts 3-4) predicts P(A) in [0.58, 0.82]. Non-overlapping boxes: observed P(A) <= 0.55 falsifies SWC's entire parameter space.

(3) FIVE-VS-ONE (E2, E2m). The five most valid experts versus the single least valid expert: NVW predicts the validity winner with P in [0.62, 0.97]; SWC's flat + vnorm components nearly cancel its recency component, so its box STRADDLES chance (P(validity winner) in [0.42, 0.58]). Observed P > 0.6 for the five-expert side is impossible for SWC at any admissible parameter combination.

(4) CUE-MIGRATION PAIR (S3 vs S4). Moving expert 3 (v = 0.85) from the early side to the late side flips NVW's sign (d: -1.00 to +0.70; predicted P(A) crosses 0.5 between adjacent trial types) while leaving SWC's prediction on the SAME side (d approx 1.0 to 1.3, both strongly pro-late-block). A sign-crossing between S3 and S4 is a qualitative signature only NVW produces.

(5) AGREEMENT ANCHORS (A1/A1m total splits; S4/S4m). Both theories agree; they establish that subjects can perform the task and calibrate overall consistency. Note the confidence dissociation: because of capacity interference, NVW's maximum predicted probability on any non-total trial is approx 0.8-0.9, whereas SWC predicts up to 0.93-0.97 on recency-unbalanced trials — the joint profile 'validity-ordered choices at moderate consistency' is uniquely NVW; 'recency-ordered choices at high consistency' is uniquely SWC.

Every conflict type appears in A/B-mirrored form to absorb side and position bias. With 24 unique pairs, K = 96 // 24 = 4 repetitions in randomized order = exactly 96 trials. Summary of decisive, parameter-free signatures: (i) on 16 sign-flip trials the theories predict opposite choices with non-overlapping probability boxes; (ii) on T1 NVW predicts exactly chance where SWC's box excludes chance; (iii) on E2 SWC's box is confined to near-chance where NVW predicts high confidence; (iv) the S3->S4 sign crossing is NVW-only; (v) regressing P(A) on validity-weighted evidence (sum v_j*s_j) versus recency-weighted evidence (sum (j/5)^3*s_j) — anti-correlated by construction — identifies which profile subjects use, with opposite regression signs under the two theories.

metric.metric_source:
def metric(data: pd.DataFrame) -> float:
    # Validity-adherence rate on VALIDITY-vs-RECENCY conflict trials.
    #
    # For every trial we compute two decision variables from the presented
    # cue patterns:
    #   d_v = sum_j v_j * sign(A_j - B_j)   (validity-weighted evidence for A)
    #   d_r = sum_j (j/(n-1))^3 * sign(A_j - B_j)  (convex cue-order recency
    #                                              evidence for A)
    # A trial is a CONFLICT trial when the two point in opposite directions
    # and both are non-trivial in magnitude. On those trials the metric is
    # the proportion of choices that follow the VALIDITY-implied option.
    #
    # NVW (validity-weighted integration) predicts adherence clearly above
    # chance (~0.6); SWC (recency-dominated subjective weights) predicts
    # adherence well below chance (~0.3), because on these trials its
    # recency gradient favors the opposite option.

    validities = np.array([0.95, 0.90, 0.85, 0.62, 0.50, 0.50], dtype=float)
    n = int(validities.shape[0])
    # Convex recency profile over presentation positions (eta ~ 3).
    recency = (np.arange(n, dtype=float) / float(n - 1)) ** 3.0

    a_col = data["option_a_ratings"]
    b_col = data["option_b_ratings"]
    r_col = data["response"]

    hits = []
    for a_raw, b_raw, resp in zip(a_col, b_col, r_col):
        a = np.asarray(a_raw, dtype=float).ravel()
        b = np.asarray(b_raw, dtype=float).ravel()
        if a.shape[0] != n or b.shape[0] != n:
            continue
        s = np.sign(a - b)
        if not np.any(s != 0):
            continue

        d_v = float(np.dot(validities, s))
        d_r = float(np.dot(recency, s))

        # Need a real conflict with non-trivial evidence on both axes.
        if abs(d_v) < 0.30 or abs(d_r) < 0.50:
            continue
        if np.sign(d_v) == np.sign(d_r):
            continue

        validity_winner_is_a = (d_v > 0.0)
        chose_a = (int(resp) == 0)
        hits.append(1.0 if (chose_a == validity_winner_is_a) else 0.0)

    if len(hits) == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(np.mean(hits))
metric.rationale:
CORE CONTRAST. Because validities are presented in strictly decreasing order, the validity-weighted evidence (d_v = sum v_j*s_j) and the convex cue-order recency evidence (d_r = sum (j/5)^3*s_j) are anti-correlated by construction. The 24-trial design contains 18 'conflict' trials where the two decision variables have opposite signs and both are non-trivial (|d_v| >= 0.3, |d_r| >= 0.5): e.g., trial 13 (A wins experts 1-2, B wins expert 6: d_v = +1.35, d_r = -0.99), trial 19 (A wins experts 1,3 vs B's 5,6: d_v = +0.80, d_r = -1.45), trial 3/5/9/11 and all their A/B mirrors. On exactly these trials the two theories make opposite parameter-free predictions: NVW's weights follow communicated validity (its integration term sigmoid(beta_eff*d_v) and its one-reason term, keyed to the top cue, both favor the validity-implied option), while SWC's recency gradient (w_6 >= 0.64 vs w_1 <= 0.19 across its entire box) favors the late-block option, i.e., the anti-validity side.

METRIC. The metric is simply the proportion of choices that agree with the validity-implied option on those conflict trials (72 observations per subject: 18 trial types x 4 repetitions). It is a plain behavioral summary — 'do subjects follow the communicated validities when validity and recency disagree?' — not a re-implementation of either model.

PREDICTED VALUES. NVW: per-trial adherence sigmoid(beta_eff*|d_v|) with beta_eff in [0.16, 0.99] gives per-trial values 0.54-0.80, aggregate ~0.60-0.65 (worst-case corner ~0.54). SWC: per-trial adherence 1 - sigmoid(beta*|d_swc|) with d_swc recency-dominated gives per-trial values ~0.10-0.45 on the 2-vs-1 and 3-vs-2 cue trials (aggregate ~0.28-0.35; even its most validity-friendly corner stays ~0.42). The gap in means is ~0.3.

WHY IT SURVIVES THE N=25 TEST. Each subject contributes 72 binary conflict observations, so pure binomial per-subject SD is ~0.055-0.06; adding parameter heterogeneity across simulated subjects keeps per-subject SD ~0.08 (variance ~0.006). With a mean gap of ~0.3, Welch's t at N=25 is roughly 0.3 / sqrt(2*0.006/25) ≈ 9-14, far below the alpha=0.01 threshold, and even the joint worst-case corners of both parameter boxes (noisiest NVW vs most validity-friendly SWC) still leave a gap of ~0.12 with t ≈ 7. Mirror trials cancel side/position bias, and the |d_v| threshold removes the validity-tie trial (d_v ≈ 0) where 'validity winner' is arbitrary. The metric works identically on the pooled DataFrame and on single-subject slices, so between-subject variance is well defined.

proposer_theory.description: Noisy Validity-weighted evidence integration with capacity-interference and one-reason lapses (NVW). People do not use a single fixed heuristic; they pool all the expert ratings they can, but each cue's contribution is weighted by its validity raised to a steepness exponent gamma (gamma = 0 recovers Tallying, gamma -> infinity recovers Take-The-Best, so both classic heuristics are limiting cases). Integration is capacity-limited: beyond a working-memory span of about four cues, every additional cue that must be pooled multiplies the reliability (effective inverse temperature) of the integrated comparison by an interference factor delta < 1, so choice consistency is design-dependent and falls sharply as feature count grows. Each cue is additionally attended only with probability alpha (lapses of attention). On a minority of trials — with a probability omega that is modulated by how strongly the most valid discriminating cue's validity dominates the validity of the opposing side's cues — the agent abandons integration and makes a one-reason decision based solely on that top cue. The final choice is a softmax (at the capacity-scaled inverse temperature) over the attended, validity-weighted evidence difference, mixed with an independent lapse to uniform guessing.
proposer_theory.predict_source:
def predict(parameters, state, history):
    # NVW: Noisy Validity-weighted integration with capacity-interference
    # and one-reason lapses.
    # Stimulus: array of shape (2, n_features); row 0 = option A, row 1 = B.
    stim = np.asarray(state, dtype=float)
    if stim.ndim != 2 or stim.shape[0] != 2:
        raise ValueError(
            f"NVW expects a (2, n_features) stimulus; got shape {stim.shape}."
        )
    a, b = stim[0], stim[1]
    n = int(stim.shape[1])

    v = np.asarray(parameters["validities"], dtype=float).ravel()
    if v.shape[0] != n:
        raise ValueError(
            f"validities length {v.shape[0]} != n_features {n}."
        )

    gamma = float(parameters["gamma"])
    alpha = float(parameters["alpha"])
    beta = float(parameters["beta"])
    delta = float(parameters["delta"])
    epsilon = float(parameters["epsilon"])
    omega_base = float(parameters["omega_base"])
    omega_dom = float(parameters["omega_dom"])

    # (1) Validity-steepness weights: gamma = 0 -> Tallying (equal weights),
    # gamma -> infinity -> Take-The-Best (top cue only).
    w = np.power(v, gamma)

    # (3) Attention: each cue independently attended with probability alpha.
    att = np.random.random(n) < alpha
    a_win = (a > b) & att
    b_win = (b > a) & att
    disc = a_win | b_win

    # (3) Capacity / interference: beyond a working-memory span of ~4 cues,
    # each additional cue that must be pooled multiplies the reliability
    # (effective inverse temperature) of the integrated evidence by delta.
    # This makes decision noise grow with feature count.
    excess = max(0, n - 4)
    beta_eff = beta * (delta ** excess)

    def _sig(z):
        # Numerically stable logistic.
        return 0.5 * (1.0 + np.tanh(0.5 * np.asarray(z, dtype=float)))

    if not np.any(disc):
        # No attended discriminating cue: pure guess.
        p_a = 0.5
    else:
        # (1) Integration: softmax over the weighted evidence difference.
        d = float(np.sum(w[a_win]) - np.sum(w[b_win]))
        p_int = float(_sig(beta_eff * d))

        # (2) One-reason mode: the single most valid attended
        # discriminating cue decides (TTB-like), with confidence scaled
        # by that cue's weight and the effective sensitivity.
        idx = np.where(disc)[0]
        top = int(idx[np.argmax(v[idx])])
        s = 1.0 if a[top] > b[top] else -1.0
        p_1r = float(_sig(beta_eff * w[top] * s))

        # (2) Validity-dominance coupling for the one-reason lapse rate:
        # dominance of the top cue over the opposing side's cue validities.
        opp = b_win if s > 0 else a_win
        if np.any(opp):
            dom = float(v[top] - np.mean(v[opp]))
        else:
            dom = float(v[top] - 0.5)
        omega_t = float(np.clip(omega_base + omega_dom * dom, 0.0, 0.95))

        p_a = (1.0 - omega_t) * p_int + omega_t * p_1r

    probs = np.array([p_a, 1.0 - p_a], dtype=float)

    # (4) Independent lapse toward uniform guessing.
    probs = (1.0 - epsilon) * probs + epsilon * 0.5
    return probs
proposer_theory.rationale:
DIAGNOSIS OF PRIOR FAILURES. TTB (pi_1) predicts P(choose TTB winner | conflict) = 0.84 in Experiment 1 (real: 0.208) and a strongly negative tally-minus-TTB contrast of -0.48 in Experiment 2 (real: +0.158): it is far too one-reason driven. Tallying (pi_2) is almost right in Experiment 1 (0.136 vs 0.208, i.e. tally-consistency 0.86 vs real 0.79) but predicts the SAME invariant consistency in Experiment 2 (0.548 vs real 0.158, i.e. tally-consistency 0.86 vs real 0.605). The signature of the human data is therefore: (i) mostly integration, mildly validity-sensitive (slightly more TTB-leaning than pure tallying in Exp 1), and (ii) a large DROP in integration consistency when the cue set grows from 5 to 6 features. Crucially, I verified analytically that the two designs are matched on every conflict-trial statistic that a fixed-noise integrator sees (weighted margins, SNR, dominance of the top cue — if anything top-cue dominance is HIGHER in Exp 1), so no shared-parameter validity weighting alone can produce the gap; the gap must be carried by a feature-count-dependent noise term. This is exactly the arbiter's mechanism (3): 'effective decision noise grows with feature count'.

MECHANISMS. NVW implements the arbiter's prescription: (1) weights w_j = v_j^gamma nest Tallying (gamma=0) and TTB (gamma->inf); (2) a one-reason lapse mode with rate omega coupled to the validity dominance of the top discriminating cue over the opposing majority's cues; (3) cue-wise attention alpha plus a capacity/interference term: beyond a working-memory span of ~4 cues, each extra pooled cue multiplies evidence reliability by delta, so noise grows steeply with feature count; (4) softmax response rule with inverse temperature beta plus an independent lapse epsilon.

CALIBRATION LOGIC. Because parameters are sampled per subject from the declared ranges and metrics are computed on the pooled population, the ranges themselves are the population-level fit (this is visible in pi_2: its 0.86 tally-consistency in BOTH experiments equals 1 - E[epsilon]/2 under uniform sampling of epsilon in [0, 0.5]). I therefore derived the ranges analytically from the conflict-trial structure of both designs so that the SAME parameter distribution reproduces both targets: with gamma ~ U[0.7, 1.3], beta ~ U[5, 11], delta ~ U[0.18, 0.30], the effective Exp-1 sensitivity is beta*delta (mean ~1.9) and the effective Exp-2 sensitivity is beta*delta^2 (mean ~0.47). Averaging the logistic over these ranges yields Exp-1 tally-consistency ~0.79-0.80 (metric P(TTB winner|conflict) ~ 0.20-0.22, real 0.208) and Exp-2 tally-consistency ~0.60-0.61 (metric ~0.15-0.17, real 0.158). The one-reason lapse (omega ~ 0.02) and lapse (epsilon ~ 0.03) contribute the small residual top-cue choices without materially shifting the averages. This is why I propose tighter ranges than the arbiter's illustrative ones: under per-subject uniform sampling, wide ranges (e.g. gamma in [0,4]) would average TTB-like and tally-like subjects and destroy the fit; the ranges above are centered on the region that both experiments jointly identify.

DEVIATION FROM ARBITER DETAIL. I keep the validity-dominance coupling for omega but let its slope (omega_dom) be free-signed: computing actual dominance values (top-cue validity minus mean opposing validity) gives a HIGHER mean in Exp 1 (0.23) than Exp 2 (0.19), so an increasing-with-dominance coupling would push Experiment 1 toward TTB — the opposite of what the data show. The between-experiment gap is instead carried by the capacity-interference term, which is the arbiter's own mechanism (3). The coupling remains in the model, falsifiable against new designs that manipulate the validity gap at fixed tally margins.

FALSIFIABLE PREDICTIONS. NVW predicts (a) choice consistency falls sharply (geometrically) as feature count grows beyond ~4 at fixed tally margins — distinguishing it from Tallying's invariance; (b) deviations from tally invariance that grow with the validity spread of the cues (via gamma); (c) a small, validity-dominance-modulated minority of pure one-reason choices. It can be validated on new designs that independently manipulate feature count and the top-cue validity gap.

experiment.rationale:
GOAL: dissociate SWC (convex cue-order recency, deterministic attention, no capacity limit) from NVW (validity^gamma weighting, capacity interference, span ~4). Prior design [4] used strictly decreasing validities, making recency and validity ANTI-correlated everywhere. This design takes the opposite, novel route: a NON-MONOTONE validity profile [0.60, 0.96, 0.60, 0.60, 0.60, 0.60, 0.90] with two high-validity peaks at positions 2 and 7 and five equal low-validity cues. This decorrelates validity from recency (rather than anti-correlating it), so each axis can be isolated in pure form, and it lets the CONVEXITY of SWC's recency gradient (eta in [2.5,4.5]: the last cue's weight is ~2x the second-to-last's and ~10x the third-to-last's) fight NVW's validity MASS head-to-head. n_features = 7 also puts three cues beyond NVW's span-4, engaging its capacity interference (beta_eff = beta*delta^3 <= 0.30), while SWC's beta is design-independent. All boxes below were verified at the corners of BOTH parameter spaces.

AXIS 1 - EQUAL-VALIDITY RECENCY LADDER (T4/T5/T6 + mirrors): A wins expert 1 (60%), B wins exactly one equally-valid (60%) expert at position 4, 5, or 6. NVW's evidence is EXACTLY zero for every parameter value (equal validities => equal weights v^gamma, symmetric attention/lapses), so NVW predicts exactly 50/50 on all six trials - parameter-free. SWC's recency gradient predicts a monotone ladder below 0.5 for the early-cue option: P(A) boxes [0.42,0.49] (vs p4), [0.30,0.43] (vs p5), [0.17,0.31] (vs p6). Observed P(later expert's product) > 0.60 on T6 is impossible for NVW at ANY admissible parameter combination, and required by SWC. This is the single cleanest trial family: pure recency with validity perfectly controlled.

AXIS 2 - HEAD-TO-HEAD DUELS (D1/D2 + mirrors): D1: A wins expert 2 (96%), B wins expert 7 (90%). NVW follows validity: P(A) in [0.50, 0.53]. SWC's convex recency makes the LAST cue dominate: P(A) in [0.14, 0.38]. Opposite signs, non-overlapping boxes - the subject prefers the product endorsed by the slightly LESS accurate but LATER expert iff SWC is true. D2 sharpens it: 96% expert 2 vs 60% expert 6 - a huge validity gap that NVW respects (P(A) in [0.50,0.54]) but SWC's recency overrides (P(A) in [0.31,0.46]). These flips survive even if NVW's capacity interference were removed (delta=1): NVW would just become more confident in the validity winner; the sign disagreement is structural.

AXIS 3 - CONVEXITY vs VALIDITY MASS (C1, L1-L4, E2 + mirrors): C1: A wins expert 7 (90%) alone; B wins experts 2+4 (96%+60%). NVW: validity mass favors B, P(A) in [0.43,0.50]; SWC: the last cue's convex weight beats both, P(A) in [0.59,0.80]. The L-ladder measures the crossover count: A wins expert 7 vs B wins k of the mid cues {3,4,5,6}. NVW's validity arithmetic says the 90% cue beats exactly ONE 60% cue (d=+0.23 at k=1, d=-0.47 at k=2), so NVW crosses 0.5 between L1 and L2. SWC's convex gradient says the last cue outweighs three mid cues (recency sum at k=3 is 0.40-0.60 < 1.0), crossing only at k=4 - a measured crossover-count dissociation of 2-3 opposing cues. E2 is the block-level flip: A wins the 3 late cues (incl. only the 90%), B wins 4 early cues (incl. the 96%): NVW says B (P(A) in [0.42,0.50]), SWC says A (P(A) in [0.71,0.94]).

AXIS 4 - CAPACITY CLIFF / CONFIDENCE (E1 + mirror): A wins experts 4-7, B wins 1-3. Both theories favor A in direction, but NVW's beta_eff <= 0.30 caps its P(A) at ~[0.50,0.56] on EVERY trial in this design (max |beta_eff*d| ~ 0.55), while SWC predicts [0.75,0.95]. Observed accuracy > 0.70 on E1 falsifies NVW's entire parameter space; near-chance performance everywhere with a residual validity-ordering falsifies SWC.

Aggregate signature: regressing P(A) on recency-weighted evidence sum((j/6)^3.5 * s_j) versus validity-weighted evidence sum(v^gamma * s_j) - decorrelated here by construction (expert 2: high validity, negligible recency; expert 6: low validity, high recency) - yields opposite-loading profiles under the two theories. Every trial type appears in A/B-mirrored form to absorb side/position bias. 24 unique pairs, K = 96//24 = 4 repetitions in randomized order = exactly 96 trials per subject.

metric.metric_source:
def metric(data: pd.DataFrame) -> float:
    # Recency-consistency rate: fraction of choices aligned with a convex
    # cue-order recency gradient, restricted to trials where that gradient
    # is strong and its direction is unambiguous across SWC's eta range.
    #
    # SWC (advocated): late cues dominate via convex recency -> rate well
    #   above 0.5 (predicted ~0.65-0.85 across its parameter box).
    # NVW (competing): validity-weighted integration with capacity
    #   interference (beta_eff = beta*delta^3 <= ~0.30 at n=7) -> choices
    #   near chance on nearly every trial, and anti-recency or neutral on
    #   the conflict trials -> rate ~0.50.
    df = data.reset_index(drop=True)
    if len(df) == 0:
        return 0.5

    a_arrs = [np.asarray(list(x), dtype=float) for x in df['option_a_ratings']]
    b_arrs = [np.asarray(list(x), dtype=float) for x in df['option_b_ratings']]
    resp = pd.to_numeric(df['response'], errors='coerce').to_numpy()

    if len(a_arrs) == 0 or a_arrs[0].ndim != 1:
        return 0.5
    n = int(a_arrs[0].shape[0])
    if n < 2:
        return 0.5

    pos = np.arange(n, dtype=float) / (n - 1.0)
    w_lo = pos ** 2.5   # SWC's eta lower corner
    w_mid = pos ** 3.5  # SWC's eta midpoint
    w_hi = pos ** 4.5   # SWC's eta upper corner

    consistent = []
    for a, b, r in zip(a_arrs, b_arrs, resp):
        if a.shape[0] != n or b.shape[0] != n:
            continue
        if not np.isfinite(r):
            continue
        s = np.sign(a - b)
        if not np.any(s != 0):
            continue
        e_lo = float(np.dot(w_lo, s))
        e_mid = float(np.dot(w_mid, s))
        e_hi = float(np.dot(w_hi, s))
        # Require the recency gradient's direction to be invariant across
        # SWC's whole eta range (drops ambiguous trials, e.g. 1 late cue vs
        # 4 mid cues, where the sign flips with eta).
        if e_lo == 0.0 or e_hi == 0.0 or np.sign(e_lo) != np.sign(e_hi):
            continue
        # Require non-trivial gradient magnitude (drops near-degenerate
        # trials where even SWC predicts ~0.52).
        if abs(e_mid) < 0.25:
            continue
        fav_a = e_mid > 0.0
        chose_a = (int(r) == 0)  # response: 0 = chose A, 1 = chose B
        consistent.append(1.0 if (chose_a == fav_a) else 0.0)

    if len(consistent) == 0:
        return 0.5
    return float(np.mean(consistent))
metric.rationale: The metric is the fraction of choices consistent with a convex cue-order recency gradient (position weights (j/(n-1))^eta), computed only on trials where (a) the gradient's preferred option is invariant across SWC's entire eta range [2.5, 4.5] and (b) its mid-range evidence magnitude is at least 0.25. In this design that admits 20 of the 24 trial types (the equal-validity recency ladder T3-T6, the validity-vs-recency duels T7-T12, the late-cue-mass trials T13-T18, and the block-level flips T21-T24), while excluding only the degenerate cue-1-vs-cue-4 trials and the eta-ambiguous 1-late-vs-4-mid trials. Mirroring in the design makes the recency-favored option A on exactly half the included trials, so side bias cancels. Predicted separation: under SWC, the per-trial probability of choosing the late-cue-endorsed product ranges from ~0.55 (worst-case corner beta=0.8, eta=2.5) to ~0.9, averaging ~0.70-0.75, so the metric lands ~0.65-0.85. Under NVW, capacity interference forces beta_eff = beta*delta^3 <= ~0.30 at n_features=7, so its logistic outputs stay within ~0.5 +/- 0.07 of chance on every trial in this design, and on the conflict trials its residual validity-ordering is anti-recency; its expected rate is ~0.49-0.51 with pure binomial noise. The gap (~0.2+ in means) is large relative to per-subject binomial noise over ~80 scored trials (sd ~0.05), so with N=25 the Welch t-test separates the theories by many sigma. The metric works identically on a single subject's slice (same trial filtering), so between-subject variance is well-defined.

proposer_theory.description: Subjective-Weighted Counting with convex cue-order recency (SWC), deterministic-attention variant. People integrate ALL discriminating cues additively with no capacity interference, but the cue weights are subjective and only partially calibrated to communicated validities: w_j = (1-lambda)/n + lambda*[(1-rho)*vnorm_j + rho*(j/(n-1))^eta]. Because validities are always presented in strictly decreasing feature order, the convex recency gradient is anti-correlated with validity, producing within-margin anti-validity preferences (Experiment 3's negative d-coefficient) while preserving mostly-tally aggregate behavior. Attention to cues is deterministic (every cue is always attended); the only stochasticity is the logistic choice noise itself plus a small uniform lapse epsilon. This edition implements the critic's in-family tuning: the noise channels that let the fit collapse to flat counting are removed or tightened so the recency gradient must do the work.

def predict(parameters, state, history):
    # SWC: Subjective-Weighted Counting with convex cue-order recency
    # (deterministic-attention variant).
    # Stimulus: array of shape (2, n_features); row 0 = option A, row 1 = B.
    stim = np.asarray(state, dtype=float)
    if stim.ndim != 2 or stim.shape[0] != 2:
        raise ValueError(
            f"SWC expects a (2, n_features) stimulus; got shape {stim.shape}."
        )
    a, b = stim[0], stim[1]
    n = int(stim.shape[1])

    v = np.asarray(parameters["validities"], dtype=float).ravel()
    if v.shape[0] != n:
        # Graceful fallback: linearly decreasing validities.
        v = np.linspace(0.95, 0.55, n)

    lam = float(parameters["lambda"])
    rho = float(parameters["rho"])
    eta = float(parameters["eta"])
    beta = float(parameters["beta"])
    eps = float(parameters["epsilon"])

    # (1) Subjective validity component: min-max normalized validities.
    vspan = float(v.max() - v.min())
    if vspan > 1e-12:
        vnorm = (v - v.min()) / vspan
    else:
        vnorm = np.full(n, 0.5)

    # (2) Recency component: position in presentation order, convexly
    # transformed so that late cues can be strongly overweighted.
    if n > 1:
        pos = (np.arange(n, dtype=float) / (n - 1.0)) ** eta
    else:
        pos = np.full(n, 0.5)

    # Subjective weights: mixture of flat counting, validity-following,
    # and recency-following. Because validities are presented in strictly
    # decreasing feature order, the recency part is anti-correlated with
    # validity -- the source of within-margin anti-validity preferences.
    g = (1.0 - rho) * vnorm + rho * pos
    w = (1.0 - lam) / n + lam * g

    # (3) Deterministic attention: every cue is attended on every trial
    # (per-cue attention lapse removed -- real subjects are highly
    # consistent, and stochastic lapses were the dominant noise source
    # inflating between-subject variance).
    s = np.sign(a - b)

    # Additive integration of all discriminating cues.
    # NO capacity interference: beta is design-independent.
    d = float(np.sum(w * s))

    # Numerically stable logistic.
    p_a = 0.5 * (1.0 + np.tanh(0.5 * beta * d))
    probs = np.array([p_a, 1.0 - p_a], dtype=float)

    # (4) Independent uniform lapse.
    probs = (1.0 - eps) * probs + eps * 0.5
    return probs
proposer_theory.rationale: Minimal-diff edit of the accepted SWC base, applying the critic's four in-family prescriptions. (1) CUT THE NOISE: the per-cue stochastic attention (alpha drawn per trial) was removed entirely — every cue is now always attended. This was the dominant variance source behind Experiment 3's between-subject variance of 0.2046 (real: 0.0186): binomial per-cue dropout made single subjects wildly inconsistent and let the fit soften aggregate rates with noise instead of using the recency gradient. The uniform lapse epsilon is retained but tightened to [0, 0.03]. (2) FORCE THE RECENCY GRADIENT TO ENGAGE: lambda is now [0.8, 1.0], rho [0.8, 1.0], eta [2.5, 4.5], so the flat-counting collapse (lambda ~ 0) that produced Exp 3 ~ 0 is unreachable; the mixture is always dominated by the graded (validity + convex recency) component. (3) MODERATE BETA: beta is capped at 1.7 (previous range went to 8), so conflict probabilities stay in the 0.6-0.9 band rather than saturating — this is what Experiment 2's near-indifferent contrast (real 0.158) requires. (4) ANCHORS: with no interference and moderate beta, hand computation at the range midpoint (lambda~0.9, rho~0.9, eta~3.5, beta~1.2) gives: Exp 4 anchor allegiance ~0.83 (real 0.843) — the 7-1 anchors with the loss on the last cue land near p~0.65, cooling the previous 0.900; Exp 1 TTB-adherence ~0.21 (real 0.208); Exp 2 contrast ~0.19-0.21 (real 0.158, down from 0.321); Exp 3 partial d-coefficient ~ -0.4 at the midpoint and ~ -0.55 to -0.68 at the recency-heavy corner (rho -> 1, lambda -> 1, beta ~1.2-1.3), bracketing the real -0.5756 — a massive improvement over the previous +0.026. The convex recency term is preserved unchanged: it remains the only in-family degree of freedom that yields Experiment 3's negative within-margin coefficient while keeping Experiments 1, 2 and 4 near their targets, and the tightened ranges now force the fit into that basin instead of the noise-dominated flat-counting region the previous parameterization permitted.

next_theory.description: INVERTED-VALIDITY COUNTING (IVC) — distrust-weighted tallying. Subjects do read the communicated validities but map them through a systematic distrust inversion: they act as if each stated validity were the expert's error rate, so the most highly validated experts are discounted most. Every discriminating cue is attended deterministically (no attention lapses, no working-memory capacity interference — choice consistency is design-independent). Each cue j carries subjective weight w_j = (1-tau)/n + tau*(1-v_j)^kappa / Z, a mixture of flat counting and a normalized inverted-validity kernel; tau is the trust placed in the inversion, kappa its steepness (kappa=0, tau=0 recovers plain Tallying; large kappa approaches a worst-expert-first one-reason rule). Evidence is integrated additively, d = sum_j w_j * sign(A_j - B_j), and the choice is a logistic function of beta*d plus a small uniform lapse epsilon. Because the anti-validity signature is grounded in the communicated validity values rather than in cue position, it transfers across designs with different validity-position layouts — unlike SWC's recency gradient, which sign-failed the recency-consistency experiment.

    n = int(stim.shape[1])

    if v.shape[0] != n:

    kappa = float(parameters["kappa"])

    # (anchor consistency stays high even at n = 8 features).

next_theory.rationale: IVC implements the arbiter's prescribed mechanism family faithfully, with parameter bounds chosen from a trial-by-trial quantitative analysis of all six displayed experiments. (1) Why inverted validity: the pooled data demand anti-validity weighting — displayed Exp 1's below-chance TTB adherence (0.208) on conflicts where the tally majority rests on low-validity cues; displayed Exp 3's strongly negative within-margin validity coefficient (-0.576), which I verified requires steep inversion (kappa >= 2.3) plus moderate beta (~2.1) to reach about -0.5; displayed Exp 5's below-chance validity adherence on validity-vs-recency conflicts (0.231), which I verified IVC reproduces (about 0.24) because inverted weights side with the recency-implied option; and displayed Exp 2's mildly positive tally-minus-TTB (0.158), where IVC lands at about 0.26, the top of the arbiter's band — lowering beta to hit it exactly would break Exps 1/3/4, so I accept this as the single residual error. (2) Why no capacity interference: displayed Exp 4's 0.843 anchor consistency at n=8 forbids it (this is what degenerated NVW to chance, 0.530); deterministic attention plus design-independent beta keeps anchors at 0.78-0.85. (3) Why no position gradient: SWC's recency gradient sign-failed displayed Exp 6 (0.726 vs 0.374); in that experiment the late cues carry high validities (0.90/0.96) and therefore receive the smallest inverted weights, so IVC stays mildly anti-recency (about 0.35-0.45) — the anti-validity signature is carried by the validity values themselves, making the theory experiment-invariant rather than order-dependent. (4) Box calibration: I computed each metric at box corners and center — the center (tau=0.925, kappa=2.7, beta=2.15, eps=0.05) yields approximately Exp1 0.20 (real 0.208), Exp2 0.26 (real 0.158), Exp3 -0.51 (real -0.576), Exp4 0.78-0.85 (real 0.843), Exp5 0.25 (real 0.231), Exp6 0.35-0.45 (real 0.374) — a strictly better error profile than the running candidates (pi_2's errors of +0.39/+0.57/+0.35 on Exps 2/3/5; pi_4's +0.16/+0.35 on Exps 3/6), while remaining inside every range the arbiter prescribed (tau in [0.3,1], kappa in [0.5,3], beta in [1,12], epsilon in [0.01,0.10]). The tight box also keeps between-subject metric variance low, matching the small observed variances.

experiment.rationale:
STRUCTURAL LEVER. IVC's weights are a function of the validity VALUES ONLY (w_j proportional to (1-v_j)^kappa: the LESS valid the expert, the MORE weight), with zero position sensitivity. SWC's weights are dominated by POSITION (convex recency, coefficient lam*rho >= 0.64, plus a weak POSITIVE validity component <= 0.20). I therefore use a non-monotone, duplicated validity profile v = [0.55, 0.90, 0.60, 0.95, 0.55, 0.60] (n=6): the two lowest validities sit at positions 1 and 5, duplicated 0.55s at positions 1/5 and duplicated 0.60s at positions 3/6, and the two highest validities at positions 2 and 4. The duplicates create validity-MATCHED comparisons at different positions (killing the validity axis and isolating pure recency), and the low-early/high-late arrangement makes IVC's weight profile (early-heavy) anti-aligned with SWC's (late-heavy). All boxes below were verified at the corners of BOTH parameter spaces.

AXIS 1 - VALIDITY-MATCHED RECENCY BATTERY (EQ1-EQ4 + mirrors). EQ1: A wins expert 1 vs B wins expert 5 (0.55 vs 0.55). EQ2: expert 3 vs expert 6 (0.60 vs 0.60). EQ3: A wins {1,3} vs B wins {5,6} (validity multiset {0.55,0.60} on BOTH sides). EQ4: A wins {1,6} vs B wins {3,5} (same matched multiset). Because IVC's weights depend only on validity values, d = 0 EXACTLY on all four -> IVC predicts P(A) = 0.50 PARAMETER-FREE. SWC's recency gradient predicts a wide spread: P(A) boxes [0.28,0.45] (EQ1), [0.12,0.39] (EQ2), [0.08,0.34] (EQ3), [0.61,0.69] (EQ4). Observed P(EQ3) <= 0.40 or P(EQ4) >= 0.55 is impossible for IVC at ANY parameter combination; observed P(EQ3) >= 0.45 is impossible for SWC. SWC requires an EQ3-vs-EQ4 spread >= 0.27 where IVC requires exactly 0.

AXIS 2 - POSITION-TRANSFER PAIRS (IVC invariance vs SWC flip). TP1: A wins expert 1 (0.55) vs B wins expert 6 (0.60). TP2: A wins expert 5 (0.55) vs B wins expert 3 (0.60). Identical validity allegiances, opposite position allegiances: IVC predicts EXACTLY the same P(A) on both, in [0.52, 0.55]; SWC predicts P(TP1) in [0.12, 0.37] (expert 6's recency dominates) and P(TP2) in [0.54, 0.69] (expert 5 beats expert 3 on recency) - a required pair difference >= 0.17 where IVC requires exactly 0. The same logic at the extreme validity gap: TP3 (A wins expert 1 vs B wins expert 4, 0.55 vs 0.95), TP4 (A wins expert 5 vs B wins expert 4), and M1 (A wins {1,3} vs B wins {4,6}, where the two 0.60 cues cancel) all have d = w(0.55) - w(0.95) under IVC -> P(A) IDENTICAL in [0.59, 0.66] on all three; SWC predicts [0.32,0.47], [0.50,0.57], [0.08,0.33] respectively - a required spread >= 0.17 (TP4 vs M1). TP3'/TP4' repeat this with the 0.90 expert: IVC-equal [0.59,0.66]; SWC [0.42,0.50] vs [0.52,0.69]. Any observed spread within a transfer family (e.g., P(TP1) != P(TP2), or P(TP3) != P(M1)) falsifies IVC's position-invariance; flatness within families falsifies SWC's recency gradient.

AXIS 3 - SIGN-FLIP DUELS. On TP1, TP3, TP3', S3 (A wins expert 3 (0.60) vs B wins expert 4 (0.95) - an ADJACENT-position duel where the later cue is also more valid), M1 and M2 (A wins {1,3,5}, the three least valid experts, vs B wins {2,4,6}), IVC favors the early/low-validity option and SWC favors the late/high-validity option with NON-OVERLAPPING boxes: IVC [0.52,0.55] vs SWC [0.12,0.37] (TP1); IVC [0.59,0.66] vs SWC [0.32,0.47] (TP3); IVC [0.59,0.66] vs SWC [0.42,0.50] (TP3'); IVC [0.57,0.61] vs SWC [0.38,0.48] (S3); IVC [0.59,0.66] vs SWC [0.08,0.33] (M1); IVC [0.63,0.73] vs SWC [0.12,0.37] (M2). M2 is the headline block flip: the option endorsed by the three WORST experts (55/60/55) is chosen confidently only by IVC; SWC confidently picks the option endorsed by the later, more valid experts.

AXIS 4 - CUE MIGRATION (AN2 -> M2). AN2: A wins {1,3,5} vs B wins {2,4}. Adding expert 6 (a mere 60%-valid cue) to B's side yields M2. IVC predicts only a modest drop (AN2 [0.70,0.78] -> M2 [0.63,0.73], still confidently A, since expert 6's inverted weight is only ~0.21 and expert 3's cancels it); SWC predicts a catastrophic flip (AN2 [0.43,0.66] -> M2 [0.12,0.37]) because expert 6 carries the maximal recency weight. A drop exceeding ~0.3 on this single-cue migration is impossible for IVC and required by SWC.

AXIS 5 - REVERSE CONFIDENCE DISSOCIATION. AN2 (A wins {1,3,5} vs B wins {2,4}): IVC [0.70,0.78] vs SWC [0.43,0.66] - IVC more confident (and SWC's box straddles chance). AN3 (A wins {5,6} vs B wins {1,2}): IVC [0.56,0.60] vs SWC [0.66,0.86] - SWC MORE confident. The confidence ordering between AN2 and AN3 reverses between theories: IVC says P(AN2) >> P(AN3); SWC says P(AN3) > P(AN2). TOT (total split) is the agreement anchor both theories accommodate.

PARAMETRIC SIGNATURE. IVC predicts only ~7 distinct probability levels across all 32 pairs (0.50 on all EQ; one level per validity-allegiance multiset for the TP/S/M/AN families; near-1 on TOT), with EXACT equalities within families; SWC predicts a wide, position-ordered spread that breaks every equality. Regressing P(A) on inverted-validity evidence sum((1-v_j)^2.7 * s_j) versus recency evidence sum((j/5)^3.5 * s_j) yields opposite-loading profiles: the two evidence axes are decorrelated by construction (expert 1: maximal inverted weight, zero recency; expert 6: maximal recency, middling inverted weight; experts 2/4: high validity, i.e., low weight for IVC but positive validity weight for SWC). Every trial type appears in A/B-mirrored form to absorb side and position bias. 32 unique pairs, K = 96 // 32 = 3 repetitions in independently randomized order = exactly 96 trials per subject.

metric.metric_source:
def metric(data: pd.DataFrame) -> float:
    """Anti-validity vs. recency disagreement score.

    On trials where IVC's distrust-inverted weights and SWC's recency-dominated
    weights point to OPPOSITE options, report the proportion of choices that
    follow the IVC-preferred option. IVC-simulated data -> well above 0.5;
    SWC-simulated data -> well below 0.5.
    """
    data = data.reset_index(drop=True)
    if len(data) == 0:
        return 0.5

    # Build stimulus matrices without hashing any list-valued cells.
    a = np.vstack([np.asarray(r, dtype=float) for r in data["option_a_ratings"]])
    b = np.vstack([np.asarray(r, dtype=float) for r in data["option_b_ratings"]])
    n = a.shape[1]

    # Design validities (fallback mirrors both theories' graceful degradation).
    v = np.array([0.5, 0.9, 0.6, 0.95, 0.5, 0.6], dtype=float)
    if v.shape[0] != n:
        v = np.linspace(0.95, 0.55, n)

    # --- IVC weights at mid-range parameters (tau=0.925, kappa=2.7) ---
    tau, kappa = 0.925, 2.7
    inv = np.power(1.0 - v, kappa)
    Z = float(inv.sum())
    w_inv = inv / Z if Z > 1e-12 else np.full(n, 1.0 / n)
    w_ivc = (1.0 - tau) / n + tau * w_inv

    # --- SWC weights at mid-range parameters (lam=0.9, rho=0.9, eta=3.5) ---
    lam, rho, eta = 0.9, 0.9, 3.5
    vspan = float(v.max() - v.min())
    if vspan > 1e-12:
        vnorm = (v - v.min()) / vspan
    else:
        vnorm = np.full(n, 0.5)
    if n > 1:
        pos = (np.arange(n, dtype=float) / (n - 1.0)) ** eta
    else:
        pos = np.full(n, 0.5)
    g = (1.0 - rho) * vnorm + rho * pos
    w_swc = (1.0 - lam) / n + lam * g

    # Signed discriminating-cue vector per trial.
    s = np.sign(a - b)
    d_ivc = s @ w_ivc
    d_swc = s @ w_swc

    # Keep only trials where the two theories STRICTLY disagree in sign.
    # (d_ivc == 0, e.g. the validity-matched EQ trials, is excluded.)
    mask = (d_ivc * d_swc) < 0.0
    if not np.any(mask):
        return 0.5

    resp = np.asarray(data["response"].to_numpy())
    r = resp[mask]
    ivc_prefers_a = d_ivc[mask] > 0.0
    chose_ivc_preferred = np.where(ivc_prefers_a, r == 0, r == 1)
    return float(chose_ivc_preferred.mean())
metric.rationale: CORE IDEA. The design's duplicated, non-monotone validity profile makes IVC's weights (a function of validity VALUES only: heaviest on the 0.5-validity experts 1/5, then 0.6 experts 3/6, near-zero on 0.9/0.95 experts 2/4) and SWC's weights (dominated by late POSITION: expert 6 >> 5 > 4 > 2 > 3 > 1) point to OPPOSITE options on a fixed, parameter-robust set of trials. The metric recomputes both theories' evidence d = w.s from the raw ratings using mid-range parameters, keeps only trials where sign(d_IVC) and sign(d_SWC) strictly disagree, and returns the proportion of choices following the IVC-preferred option. PARAMETER ROBUSTNESS. I verified the sign of d under BOTH theories at all corners of both parameter spaces: the disagreement set is exactly 12 of the 32 trial types (trials 5, 7, 9, 11, 12, 13, 21, 23, 25, 27, 28, 29 in the design listing), i.e. 36 of each subject's 96 trials, independent of tau/kappa/beta/epsilon (IVC) and lam/rho/eta/beta/epsilon (SWC). For example, w1 < w2 always under SWC (position/validity gradient) while w(0.5) > w(0.9) always under IVC; trial 13 (A wins experts 1,3,5 vs B wins 2,4,6) pits the three least-valid experts against the three latest-position experts — IVC favors the low-validity side, SWC the late side, at every parameter corner. So the mid-parameter weights used inside the metric only need to recover the SIGNS, which are invariant. EXPECTED SEPARATION. Under IVC (mid params) the per-trial P(choose IVC-preferred) on the 12 disagreement types averages ~0.65 (rising to ~0.78 on trials 13/29); under SWC it averages ~0.36. Pooled point estimates: ~0.64 (IVC data) vs ~0.36 (SWC data), a gap of ~0.28. VARIANCE. Per subject the metric is a proportion over 36 Bernoulli trials with p near 0.65 (or 0.36), giving per-subject SD ~0.08; parameter heterogeneity across subjects adds little (the boxes are tight). Welch's t at N=25 with variances ~0.006-0.008 on each side yields t > 9, p far below 0.01. The metric works identically on a single subject's slice (36 trials, no NaN), so the between-subject variance is well defined. INTERPRETATION. A value near 0.5 means neither anti-validity nor recency dominates; >0.5 supports distrust-weighted (inverted-validity) counting; <0.5 supports position/recency-weighted counting. Because agreement trials (e.g., the total splits 16/32, and all validity-matched EQ trials where IVC is exactly at chance) are excluded, the metric carries pure discriminating signal with minimal noise.
