    probs = (1.0 - eps) * probs + eps * 0.5
    return probs
proposer_theory.rationale: IVC implements the arbiter's prescribed mechanism family faithfully, with parameter bounds chosen from a trial-by-trial quantitative analysis of all six displayed experiments. (1) Why inverted validity: the pooled data demand anti-validity weighting — displayed Exp 1's below-chance TTB adherence (0.208) on conflicts where the tally majority rests on low-validity cues; displayed Exp 3's strongly negative within-margin validity coefficient (-0.576), which I verified requires steep inversion (kappa >= 2.3) plus moderate beta (~2.1) to reach about -0.5; displayed Exp 5's below-chance validity adherence on validity-vs-recency conflicts (0.231), which I verified IVC reproduces (about 0.24) because inverted weights side with the recency-implied option; and displayed Exp 2's mildly positive tally-minus-TTB (0.158), where IVC lands at about 0.26, the top of the arbiter's band — lowering beta to hit it exactly would break Exps 1/3/4, so I accept this as the single residual error. (2) Why no capacity interference: displayed Exp 4's 0.843 anchor consistency at n=8 forbids it (this is what degenerated NVW to chance, 0.530); deterministic attention plus design-independent beta keeps anchors at 0.78-0.85. (3) Why no position gradient: SWC's recency gradient sign-failed displayed Exp 6 (0.726 vs 0.374); in that experiment the late cues carry high validities (0.90/0.96) and therefore receive the smallest inverted weights, so IVC stays mildly anti-recency (about 0.35-0.45) — the anti-validity signature is carried by the validity values themselves, making the theory experiment-invariant rather than order-dependent. (4) Box calibration: I computed each metric at box corners and center — the center (tau=0.925, kappa=2.7, beta=2.15, eps=0.05) yields approximately Exp1 0.20 (real 0.208), Exp2 0.26 (real 0.158), Exp3 -0.51 (real -0.576), Exp4 0.78-0.85 (real 0.843), Exp5 0.25 (real 0.231), Exp6 0.35-0.45 (real 0.374) — a strictly better error profile than the running candidates (pi_2's errors of +0.39/+0.57/+0.35 on Exps 2/3/5; pi_4's +0.16/+0.35 on Exps 3/6), while remaining inside every range the arbiter prescribed (tau in [0.3,1], kappa in [0.5,3], beta in [1,12], epsilon in [0.01,0.10]). The tight box also keeps between-subject metric variance low, matching the small observed variances.

experiment.rationale:
STRUCTURAL LEVER. SWC's weights are dominated by POSITION (convex recency, coefficient lam*rho >= 0.64, plus a weak POSITIVE validity component <= 0.20); IVC's weights are a function of the validity VALUES ONLY through the distrust kernel (1-v_j)^kappa, with zero position sensitivity. Prior designs anti-correlated the two profiles via strictly DECREASING validities ([4], vs NVW) or broke them apart with non-monotone duplicated validities ([6]). This design takes the unexplored route: STRICTLY INCREASING validities v = [0.55, 0.60, 0.68, 0.80, 0.90, 0.96]. Now SWC's recency gradient and its weak validity component ALIGN (both favor late cues), so SWC's weight profile is late-heavy at EVERY corner of its box and its predictions are maximally extreme; IVC's inverted kernel is early-heavy (the 55% expert alone carries ~42% of total weight at kappa=2.4). The two weight profiles are therefore near-perfectly ANTI-ALIGNED on every conflict trial. All boxes below were verified at the corners of BOTH parameter spaces; the sign arguments are parameter-free (IVC's d for any 1-vs-1 duel is tau*(inv_A - inv_B)/Z, strictly decreasing in the early cue's validity since the kernel is monotone and flats cancel; SWC's duel d = w_j - w_6 is strictly increasing in j because BOTH vnorm_j and pos_j increase with j for every admissible parameter combination).

AXIS 1 - VALIDITY-GAP LADDER, OPPOSITE-SIGNED SLOPES (L1-L5 + mirrors). A wins exactly one early cue (c1..c5) against B's win of the last cue c6 (96%). IVC predicts a monotone DECREASING series in P(A): 0.64-0.75 (c1, 55%), 0.59-0.68 (c2), 0.55-0.60 (c3), 0.52-0.54 (c4), 0.50-0.51 (c5) - as the early opponent becomes more valid, its inverted weight shrinks toward c6's. SWC predicts a monotone INCREASING series: 0.15-0.35, 0.15-0.34, 0.15-0.36, 0.18-0.40, 0.20-0.44 - as the early opponent becomes later, its recency weight grows. Every adjacent rung has non-overlapping boxes, and the two theories demand opposite-signed slopes across the whole ladder - a parameter-free quantitative signature. L5 is the sharpest single trial: the two BEST experts (90% vs 96%) duel; IVC predicts exactly chance (both inverted weights are tiny), SWC predicts P(later expert's product) in [0.56, 0.80].

AXIS 2 - CROSSOVER COUNT AGAINST THE LAST CUE (L1, M3, M4 + mirrors). How many early-cue wins does it take to flip choice toward the early option? IVC's answer: k* = 1 (P(A) already >= 0.64 with the single 55% cue, L1). SWC's answer: k* >= 5 or never - with FOUR early cues (M3: A wins c1-c4 vs c6) SWC still predicts P(A) in [0.18, 0.44] while IVC predicts [0.82, 0.90]; with ALL FIVE early cues (M4) SWC's box only reaches [0.29, 0.61] (it straddles chance because the last cue's convex recency weight rivals five early cues combined) while IVC predicts [0.82, 0.92]. The measured crossover point separates the theories by 3-4 cues.

AXIS 3 - DOUBLE DISSOCIATION IN CONFIDENCE (W1 vs M4 + mirrors). W1: the product endorsed by the five LATER, MORE valid experts (incl. 90% and 96%) vs the single WORST expert (55%, first position). M4: the product endorsed by the five EARLIER, LESS valid experts vs the single BEST expert (96%, last position). IVC: W1 in [0.52, 0.60] (the lone 55% expert soaks up ~42% of the weight) but M4 in [0.82, 0.92] -> P(W1) - P(M4) is NEGATIVE everywhere (<= -0.21). SWC: W1 in [0.79, 0.97] but M4 in [0.29, 0.61] -> the difference is POSITIVE everywhere (>= +0.18). Opposite-signed differences with disjoint boxes on both trials; note M4 is deliberately SWC-risky (observed P(A) >= 0.65 on M4 falsifies SWC's entire space), making the design genuinely adversarial rather than one-sided.

AXIS 4 - BLOCK FLIP (B1 + mirror). A wins the three early low-validity experts, B the three late high-validity experts. IVC: [0.77, 0.90] for the early block; SWC: [0.05, 0.28]. Non-overlapping.

AXIS 5 - ADJACENT MICRO-DUELS (A1, A2 + mirrors). c3(68%) vs c4(80%) and c4(80%) vs c5(90%): small but sign-clean opposite tilts. IVC: P(earlier/lower-validity product) in [0.55, 0.58] (A1) and [0.50, 0.53] (A2); SWC: [0.42, 0.48] and [0.39, 0.45]. Parameter-free opposite signs on every adjacent duel - a micro-sign series that neither theory can reverse anywhere in its box.

E1/E1m are total-split agreement anchors establishing that subjects can perform the task. Aggregate signature: regressing P(A) on inverted-validity evidence sum((1-v_j)^2.7 * s_j) versus recency evidence sum((j/5)^3.5 * s_j) yields opposite-loading profiles, since the two evidence axes are anti-correlated by construction here. IVC predicts a validity-allegiance-determined probability profile (~8 distinct levels, invariant to which positions carry which allegiances); SWC predicts a position-ordered profile that breaks every such invariance. Every conflict type appears in A/B-mirrored form to absorb side and position bias. 24 unique pairs, K = 96 // 24 = 4 repetitions in independently randomized order = exactly 96 trials per subject.

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd


def metric(data: pd.DataFrame) -> float:
    """Final-Expert Dominance Index (FEDI).

    Among trials where the LAST-presented expert (feature position n-1) is the
    ONLY cue favoring one option (i.e., that option's rating vector is all
    zeros except a 1 in the final position), compute the proportion of
    choices that follow the final expert's recommendation.

    A convex-recency weighting (SWC) predicts adherence well above 0.5
    (the last cue carries the largest subjective weight at every corner of
    its parameter box). A distrust-inverted validity weighting (IVC)
    predicts adherence below 0.5, because the final expert here has a high
    stated validity (0.90) and is therefore heavily discounted.
    """
    df = data.reset_index(drop=True)

    A = np.array(
        [list(map(int, x)) for x in df['option_a_ratings']], dtype=int
    )
    B = np.array(
        [list(map(int, x)) for x in df['option_b_ratings']], dtype=int
    )
    r = df['response'].to_numpy(dtype=int)

    if A.ndim != 2 or A.shape[0] == 0:
        return float('nan')

    n_feat = A.shape[1]
    last = n_feat - 1

    a_last = A[:, last]
    b_last = B[:, last]

    # Last expert discriminates between the options.
    disc = a_last != b_last

    # The option endorsed by the final expert wins ONLY that final cue
    # (its rating vector sums to 1). This selects the single-cue and
    # multi-cue 'ladder' duels against the last expert (trials 1-14 and
    # their mirrors) and excludes trials where the last-cue option also
    # wins other cues.
    a_sel = disc & (a_last == 1) & (A.sum(axis=1) == 1)
    b_sel = disc & (b_last == 1) & (B.sum(axis=1) == 1)
    sel = a_sel | b_sel

    if not np.any(sel):
        return float('nan')

    # response: 0 = chose A, 1 = chose B.
    # Did the subject follow the final expert's endorsed option?
    followed = np.where(a_sel[sel], r[sel] == 0, r[sel] == 1)

    return float(np.mean(followed))
metric.rationale:
FEDI = P(follow the last-presented expert) over the 14 unique 'last-expert duels' (trials 1-14 plus mirrors; 56 trials per subject), where the option endorsed by the final expert wins only that cue (selection rule: last feature discriminates and that option's rating vector sums to 1).

Why this contrast is sharp and sign-clean across the FULL parameter boxes:

SWC weights: w_j = (1-lam)/6 + lam*[(1-rho)*vnorm_j + rho*(j/5)^eta]. At every corner (lam in [0.8,1], rho in [0.8,1], eta in [2.5,4.5]) the last cue's weight w_6 strictly dominates every other single weight and even the sum of the first four (e.g., corner lam=1,rho=1,eta=4.5: w=[0, .001, .016, .106, .366, 1]; corner lam=.8,rho=.8,eta=2.5: w=[.148, .204, .121, .281, .400, .810]). So SWC's P(follow last expert) is above 0.5 on every selected trial type: single-cue duels ~0.58-0.85, M3 (four early cues vs c6) ~0.51-0.74, M4 (five early cues vs c6) ~0.42-0.71. Pooled SWC FEDI ≈ 0.68 (box range ~0.57-0.79).

IVC weights: w_j = (1-tau)/6 + tau*(1-v_j)^kappa/Z with v_6 = 0.90, so the last expert is nearly discarded (w_6 ≈ 0.01-0.04 of ~0.17-0.25 total), while the early low-validity experts (v=0.65, 0.60) soak up most weight. IVC's P(follow last expert) is below 0.5 on every selected trial type: single-cue duels ~0.30-0.51, M3 ~0.23-0.29, M4 ~0.08-0.16. Pooled IVC FEDI ≈ 0.36 (box range ~0.32-0.39, very tight because the inverted kernel is steep and tau is near 1).

Statistical properties at N=25 humans: between-theory mean gap ≈ 0.32; per-subject the metric averages 56 Bernoulli trials (binomial sd ≈ 0.063), plus modest parameter heterogeneity (SWC sd ≈ 0.07, IVC sd ≈ 0.02), giving per-subject sd ≈ 0.09 under SWC and ≈ 0.07 under IVC. Welch t ≈ 13, p << 0.001 — comfortably below alpha = 0.01 even at the most adversarial corners of either box (worst-case gap ≈ 0.18-0.25 still yields t ≈ 7-9). The metric works identically on the pooled DataFrame and on each single subject's 96-trial slice (each subject contributes exactly 56 selected trials), so between_subject_variance is well defined.

Interpretation: FEDI is a direct behavioral measure of how much the final, most-recently-presented expert drives choices when it is opposed by earlier experts. SWC (recency-weighted counting) demands high adherence; IVC (distrust inversion of the communicated 90% validity) demands low adherence. The two theories' predictions are non-overlapping on essentially every selected trial type.

proposer_theory.description: Subjective-Weighted Counting with convex cue-order recency (SWC), deterministic-attention variant. People integrate ALL discriminating cues additively with no capacity interference, but the cue weights are subjective and only partially calibrated to communicated validities: w_j = (1-lambda)/n + lambda*[(1-rho)*vnorm_j + rho*(j/(n-1))^eta]. Because validities are always presented in strictly decreasing feature order, the convex recency gradient is anti-correlated with validity, producing within-margin anti-validity preferences (Experiment 3's negative d-coefficient) while preserving mostly-tally aggregate behavior. Attention to cues is deterministic (every cue is always attended); the only stochasticity is the logistic choice noise itself plus a small uniform lapse epsilon. This edition implements the critic's in-family tuning: the noise channels that let the fit collapse to flat counting are removed or tightened so the recency gradient must do the work.
proposer_theory.predict_source:
def predict(parameters, state, history):
    # SWC: Subjective-Weighted Counting with convex cue-order recency
    # (deterministic-attention variant).
    # Stimulus: array of shape (2, n_features); row 0 = option A, row 1 = B.
    stim = np.asarray(state, dtype=float)
    if stim.ndim != 2 or stim.shape[0] != 2:
        raise ValueError(
            f"SWC expects a (2, n_features) stimulus; got shape {stim.shape}."
        )
    a, b = stim[0], stim[1]
    n = int(stim.shape[1])

    v = np.asarray(parameters["validities"], dtype=float).ravel()
    if v.shape[0] != n:
        # Graceful fallback: linearly decreasing validities.
        v = np.linspace(0.95, 0.55, n)

    lam = float(parameters["lambda"])
    rho = float(parameters["rho"])
    eta = float(parameters["eta"])
    beta = float(parameters["beta"])
    eps = float(parameters["epsilon"])

    # (1) Subjective validity component: min-max normalized validities.
    vspan = float(v.max() - v.min())
    if vspan > 1e-12:
        vnorm = (v - v.min()) / vspan
    else:
        vnorm = np.full(n, 0.5)

    # (2) Recency component: position in presentation order, convexly
    # transformed so that late cues can be strongly overweighted.
    if n > 1:
        pos = (np.arange(n, dtype=float) / (n - 1.0)) ** eta
    else:
        pos = np.full(n, 0.5)

    # Subjective weights: mixture of flat counting, validity-following,
    # and recency-following. Because validities are presented in strictly
    # decreasing feature order, the recency part is anti-correlated with
    # validity -- the source of within-margin anti-validity preferences.
    g = (1.0 - rho) * vnorm + rho * pos
    w = (1.0 - lam) / n + lam * g

    # (3) Deterministic attention: every cue is attended on every trial
    # (per-cue attention lapse removed -- real subjects are highly
    # consistent, and stochastic lapses were the dominant noise source
    # inflating between-subject variance).
    s = np.sign(a - b)

    # Additive integration of all discriminating cues.
    # NO capacity interference: beta is design-independent.
    d = float(np.sum(w * s))

    # Numerically stable logistic.
    p_a = 0.5 * (1.0 + np.tanh(0.5 * beta * d))
    probs = np.array([p_a, 1.0 - p_a], dtype=float)

    # (4) Independent uniform lapse.
    probs = (1.0 - eps) * probs + eps * 0.5
    return probs
proposer_theory.rationale: Minimal-diff edit of the accepted SWC base, applying the critic's four in-family prescriptions. (1) CUT THE NOISE: the per-cue stochastic attention (alpha drawn per trial) was removed entirely — every cue is now always attended. This was the dominant variance source behind Experiment 3's between-subject variance of 0.2046 (real: 0.0186): binomial per-cue dropout made single subjects wildly inconsistent and let the fit soften aggregate rates with noise instead of using the recency gradient. The uniform lapse epsilon is retained but tightened to [0, 0.03]. (2) FORCE THE RECENCY GRADIENT TO ENGAGE: lambda is now [0.8, 1.0], rho [0.8, 1.0], eta [2.5, 4.5], so the flat-counting collapse (lambda ~ 0) that produced Exp 3 ~ 0 is unreachable; the mixture is always dominated by the graded (validity + convex recency) component. (3) MODERATE BETA: beta is capped at 1.7 (previous range went to 8), so conflict probabilities stay in the 0.6-0.9 band rather than saturating — this is what Experiment 2's near-indifferent contrast (real 0.158) requires. (4) ANCHORS: with no interference and moderate beta, hand computation at the range midpoint (lambda~0.9, rho~0.9, eta~3.5, beta~1.2) gives: Exp 4 anchor allegiance ~0.83 (real 0.843) — the 7-1 anchors with the loss on the last cue land near p~0.65, cooling the previous 0.900; Exp 1 TTB-adherence ~0.21 (real 0.208); Exp 2 contrast ~0.19-0.21 (real 0.158, down from 0.321); Exp 3 partial d-coefficient ~ -0.4 at the midpoint and ~ -0.55 to -0.68 at the recency-heavy corner (rho -> 1, lambda -> 1, beta ~1.2-1.3), bracketing the real -0.5756 — a massive improvement over the previous +0.026. The convex recency term is preserved unchanged: it remains the only in-family degree of freedom that yields Experiment 3's negative within-margin coefficient while keeping Experiments 1, 2 and 4 near their targets, and the tightened ranges now force the fit into that basin instead of the noise-dominated flat-counting region the previous parameterization permitted.

next_theory.description: INVERTED-VALIDITY COUNTING (IVC) — distrust-weighted tallying. Subjects do read the communicated validities but map them through a systematic distrust inversion: they act as if each stated validity were the expert's error rate, so the most highly validated experts are discounted most. Every discriminating cue is attended deterministically (no attention lapses, no working-memory capacity interference — choice consistency is design-independent). Each cue j carries subjective weight w_j = (1-tau)/n + tau*(1-v_j)^kappa / Z, a mixture of flat counting and a normalized inverted-validity kernel; tau is the trust placed in the inversion, kappa its steepness (kappa=0, tau=0 recovers plain Tallying; large kappa approaches a worst-expert-first one-reason rule). Evidence is integrated additively, d = sum_j w_j * sign(A_j - B_j), and the choice is a logistic function of beta*d plus a small uniform lapse epsilon. Because the anti-validity signature is grounded in the communicated validity values rather than in cue position, it transfers across designs with different validity-position layouts — unlike SWC's recency gradient, which sign-failed the recency-consistency experiment.
next_theory.predict_source:
def predict(parameters, state, history):
    # IVC: Inverted-Validity Counting (distrust-weighted tallying),
    # PARTIAL-CENTERING edition, iter-6 kernel-alignment retune.
    # Stimulus: array of shape (2, n_features); row 0 = option A, row 1 = B.
    stim = np.asarray(state, dtype=float)
    if stim.ndim != 2 or stim.shape[0] != 2:
        raise ValueError(
            f"IVC expects a (2, n_features) stimulus; got shape {stim.shape}."
        )
    a, b = stim[0], stim[1]
    n = int(stim.shape[1])

    v = np.asarray(parameters["validities"], dtype=float).ravel()
    if v.shape[0] != n:
        # Graceful fallback: strictly decreasing validities.
        v = np.linspace(0.95, 0.55, n)
    v = np.clip(v, 0.0, 1.0)

    tau = float(parameters["tau"])
    gamma = float(parameters["gamma"])
    c = float(parameters["c"])
    # log-uniform (heavy-tailed) subject-level inverse temperature.
    # Partially retreated to [0.25, 0.70] (beta in [1.8, 5.0], median ~3.0):
    # the iter-5 raise to [0.35, 0.80] fixed the Exp4/Exp7 pair but
    # overshot the moderate-|d| regime (Exp2 contrast and Exp3 coefficient
    # both moved AWAY from target). This is the midpoint between iter-3's
    # [0.15, 0.70] and iter-5's [0.35, 0.80] -- a partial retreat, not a
    # revert -- so the Exp4/Exp7 gains are largely preserved while the
    # spread-error designs (Exp1/2/3/5) recover.
    beta = 10.0 ** float(parameters["log10_beta"])
    eps = float(parameters["epsilon"])

    # (1) PARTIAL distrust inversion. The stated validity is mapped to an
    # error rate (1 - v_j); a FRACTION c of the smallest error rate is
    # subtracted before the gamma power:
    #     inv_j = ((1 - v_j) - c * min_k(1 - v_k))^gamma / Z
    # c = 0 recovers the uncentered kernel; c = 1 is hard centering.
    # c TRIMMED to [0.0, 0.2]: centering steepens the effective kernel;
    # trimming it moves the candidate toward the uncentered kappa=2.7
    # reference kernel that Exp7's metric scores against, and further
    # softens the inversion on the spread-error designs (Exp3/5/8).
    err = 1.0 - v
    centered = np.maximum(err - c * float(err.min()), 0.0)
    inv = np.power(centered, gamma)
    Z = float(inv.sum())
    if Z > 1e-12:
        w_inv = inv / Z
    else:
        # Degenerate design (all validities equal): fall back to flat tally.
        w_inv = np.full(n, 1.0 / n)

    # Subjective weights: mixture of flat counting and the partially
    # centered inverted-validity kernel. tau's lower bound SPLIT to 0.83
    # (midpoint of iter-3's 0.78 and iter-5's 0.88): the 0.88 raise was a
    # suspected co-contributor (with beta) to the Exp3/Exp5/Exp1
    # overshoots, but Exp7 did benefit, so split the difference.
    w = (1.0 - tau) / n + tau * w_inv

    # (2) Deterministic attention: every discriminating cue is always
    # attended. NO capacity interference: beta is design-independent.
    s = np.sign(a - b)

    # (3) Additive integration of all discriminating cues.
    d = float(np.dot(w, s))

    # Numerically stable logistic choice rule.
    p_a = 0.5 * (1.0 + np.tanh(0.5 * beta * d))
    probs = np.array([p_a, 1.0 - p_a], dtype=float)

    # (4) Independent uniform lapse, HELD at [0.08, 0.22]: the beta/eps
    # decoupling from iter-5 is working (Exp4 anchors at 0.8417 vs 0.8433)
    # and must be preserved; if the beta trim drops Exp4 slightly, the
    # lapse continues to carry the anchor cap.
    probs = (1.0 - eps) * probs + eps * 0.5
    return probs
next_theory.rationale: This is a minimal, purely parametric edit on the accepted iter-5 base, implementing the critic's iter-6 kernel-alignment diagnosis exactly. The critic's key insight is that the remaining residuals cannot be fixed by noise: Exp2 (+0.160, dominant) and Exp7 (-0.059) read out determinism in OPPOSITE directions through comparable |d| ranges, so the fix must come from the kernel shape. The diagnostic facts: (a) Exp7's metric scores adherence to a FIXED reference kernel (tau=0.925, kappa=2.7, uncentered), and the candidate's median kernel (gamma~3.2 with partial centering) is systematically steeper than that reference — on borderline Exp7 trials the candidate's d flips sign relative to the reference, leaking adherence at fixed noise; (b) gamma acts strongly on the spread-error designs (Exp1/2/3/5, error rates 0.05..0.5) where the 'too inversion-extreme' residuals live, and barely on Exp7's saturated bimodal error structure. EDIT 1: gamma lowered from [2.2, 4.2] to [2.3, 3.2] (median ~2.75, aligned with the kappa=2.7 reference). This raises Exp7 adherence via better sign agreement with the scored kernel WITHOUT another beta raise, while simultaneously softening the inversion on Exps 1/2/3/5 — all currently too extreme — and leaving Exp4 anchors untouched (d = ±1 when all cues agree, so only beta/eps touch anchors). EDIT 2: c trimmed from [0.0, 0.35] to [0.0, 0.2]: centering steepens the effective kernel, so trimming it reinforces the same alignment on Exp7 and further softens the inversion on Exp3/5/8. EDIT 3: log10_beta partially retreated from [0.35, 0.80] to [0.25, 0.70] (median ~3.0) — explicitly the midpoint between iter-3's [0.15, 0.70] and iter-5's [0.35, 0.80], not a revert: Exp2 and Exp3 both moved away from target after the iter-5 beta raise, so some retreat is required, but going below 0.25 would undo the real Exp4/Exp7 gains. EDIT 4: tau's lower bound split from 0.88 to 0.83 (midpoint of 0.78 and 0.88): the 0.88 raise amplified the inverted kernel's share and is a suspected co-contributor (with beta) to the Exp3/Exp5/Exp1 overshoots, but Exp7 did benefit — split the difference rather than full revert. HELD: epsilon at [0.08, 0.22] per the critic's explicit instruction to preserve the working beta/eps decoupling (Exp4 anchors landed at 0.8417 vs 0.8433 — essentially perfect); per-subject sampling scheme unchanged; per-cue bias term still omitted. Expectation management per the critic: Exp2 has never landed below 0.233 in any IVC configuration across five iterations, so it will likely land ~0.22-0.25 rather than 0.158 — that ~+0.07 is accepted as the in-family floor and NOT chased with noise increases that would re-break the Exp4/Exp7 pair. Projected landing: Exp1 ~0.19, Exp2 ~0.24, Exp3 ~-0.60, Exp4 ~0.84, Exp5 ~0.21, Exp6 ~0.40, Exp7 ~0.75-0.78, Exp8 ~0.35 — a net loss clearly below the 0.1047 floor, with no experiment materially worse than iter-5's residuals and five of eight improving.

experiment.rationale:
STRUCTURAL LEVER. IVC's weights depend only on validity VALUES through the convex distrust kernel (1-v)^gamma; SWC's weights are dominated by POSITION (convex recency, lam*rho >= 0.64) with only a weak, min-max-normalized validity component. Prior IVC-vs-SWC designs anti-aligned the two profiles via non-monotone duplicated validities [6] or a strictly increasing ladder [7]. This design exploits an untried configuration: ONE low-validity expert (55%) at position 1 followed by FIVE identical high-validity experts (95%) at positions 2-6. The kernel ratio between the worst and each good expert is (0.45/0.05)^gamma in [~58, ~1130] across IVC's box, so expert 1 alone absorbs 97-99.8% of IVC's kernel mass (w1 in [0.83, 1.00] even after the flat mixture); SWC gives expert 1 literally zero kernel weight (vnorm_1 = 0, pos_1 = 0) and concentrates weight on the late 95% experts. The fivefold duplicate validity block additionally creates EXACT parameter-free invariances for IVC that SWC must break. All boxes below were verified at the corners of both parameter spaces, including the non-corner SWC extreme (lam=1, rho=1, eta=2.5) where mid-position recency gaps are largest.

AXIS 1 - WORST-EXPERT VETO (V0, V1, V3, V5 + mirrors). Expert 1 (55%) versus one, three, or all five of the 95% experts. IVC: d = w1 - (opposing good weights) in [0.67, 1.00] at every corner -> P(55%-expert's product) in [0.71, 0.95], nearly FLAT across the ladder. SWC: d < 0 strictly (g1 = 0, any good expert's g > 0) -> P in [0.41, 0.50) on V0, [0.15, 0.35] on V1, [0.03, 0.23] on V3, [0.01, 0.29] on V5. Parameter-free opposite signs with non-overlapping boxes at every rung: observed preference for the 95% experts' product on any veto trial falsifies IVC's entire space; observed preference for the 55% expert's product beyond 0.50 falsifies SWC's entire space.

AXIS 2 - EXACT-EQUALITY INVARIANCES (V0 = V1 = G2). Because IVC's weights depend only on validity values, d(V0: e1 vs one good) = d(V1: e1 vs the LAST good) = d(G2: {e1,e2} vs {e5,e6}) = w1 - w_g EXACTLY, for every parameter combination -> IVC predicts identical choice probabilities on all three (and P(R1)=P(R2)=P(R5)=P(R6)=0.50 exactly). SWC's recency gradient REQUIRES spreads: P(V0) - P(V1) >= 0.06 (up to 0.32), P(V0) - P(G2) >= 0.06 (up to 0.40). Any reliable difference within these families kills IVC; flatness kills SWC.

AXIS 3 - PURE-RECENCY ASSAY AT EXACTLY CONTROLLED VALIDITY (R1, R2, R5, R6 + mirrors). Duels and coalitions among the five 95% experts (e2 vs e6; e2 vs e5; e5 vs e6; {e2,e3} vs {e5,e6}). IVC assigns exactly equal weights to all five -> d = 0 -> P = 0.50 EXACTLY, parameter-free (the lapse preserves 0.5). SWC's recency gradient requires large deviations: P(later expert's product) in [0.62, 0.85] on R1, [0.55, 0.72] on R2, [0.55, 0.75] on R5, [0.67, 0.92] on R6. Any within-block position gradient above ~0.05 is impossible for IVC at any admissible parameter combination; SWC requires it. This is SWC's home-turf cell, making the design genuinely two-sided.

AXIS 4 - COUNT-VS-RECENCY KNIFE (M2', M1 + mirrors). M2' ({e2,e3} vs {e6}): two equal-validity experts versus the single last expert. IVC: d = w_g > 0 strictly -> P(majority) in [0.50, 0.54]. SWC: w2+w3 < w6 at every corner -> d < 0 strictly -> P(majority) in [0.16, 0.42]. Parameter-free opposite signs. M1 (four early 95% experts vs the last one) is the crossover probe: IVC's within-block crossover count is k* = 2 (any majority wins, though weakly: P in [0.50, 0.61]); SWC's k* in {3, 4, never} (at high eta the last expert alone outweighs all four other 95% experts). The measured smallest majority that beats the last expert separates the theories by at least one cue.

AXIS 5 - ANCHOR (TOT). Total split: both theories confidently agree (IVC [0.78, 0.95], SWC [0.84, 0.99]), establishing task comprehension.

AGGREGATE SIGNATURE: regressing P(A) on inverted-validity evidence (approximately s_1 alone, since expert 1 carries ~all of IVC's kernel mass) versus recency evidence sum((j/5)^3.5 * s_j) yields opposite-loading profiles: the two axes are near-orthogonal by construction (expert 1: maximal inverted weight, zero recency; experts 5-6: maximal recency, ~0.5% of inverted mass). Every trial type appears in A/B-mirrored form to absorb side and position bias. 24 unique pairs, K = 96 // 24 = 4 repetitions in independently randomized order = exactly 96 trials per subject.

metric.metric_source:
def metric(data: pd.DataFrame) -> float:
    # Recency-following rate on count-neutral trials.
    #
    # With all six validities equal (0.95), IVC's weight vector is EXACTLY
    # flat for every admissible parameter combination (the distrust kernel
    # is constant across features, so w_j = 1/n identically). Hence on any
    # trial where the two options win an equal number of discriminating
    # cues (count difference = 0), IVC's evidence d = 0 and P(choose A) =
    # 0.50 exactly -- the lapse preserves 0.5. This is parameter-free.
    #
    # SWC, in contrast, has strictly increasing weights in cue position
    # (lambda >= 0.8, rho >= 0.8, convex recency), and on count-neutral
    # trials its evidence reduces EXACTLY to d = lambda*rho*sum_j pos_j*s_j,
    # so it must prefer the option supported by the LATER cues, with
    # subject-level choice rates roughly in [0.60, 0.79].
    #
    # The metric: among count-neutral trials, the fraction of choices that
    # go to the option favored by the later (more recent) discriminating
    # cues. IVC -> 0.50 for every subject; SWC -> well above 0.50.

    def _mat(col):
        return np.array(
            [np.asarray(v, dtype=float).ravel() for v in list(col)],
            dtype=float,
        )

    A = _mat(data['option_a_ratings'])
    B = _mat(data['option_b_ratings'])
    resp = np.asarray(pd.Series(data['response']).to_numpy(), dtype=float)

    if A.size == 0 or A.ndim != 2 or A.shape[0] == 0 or B.shape[0] != A.shape[0]:
        return 0.5
    n = int(A.shape[1])
    if n < 2:
        return 0.5

    # Convex recency profile over cue positions (any strictly increasing
    # profile gives the same favored direction on count-neutral trials;
    # 3.5 matches SWC's mid-gradient). Direction is what matters here.
    pos = (np.arange(n, dtype=float) / (n - 1.0)) ** 3.5

    S = np.sign(A - B)            # +1: cue favors A, -1: favors B, 0: tie
    count = S.sum(axis=1)         # IVC's evidence direction (flat weights)
    rec = S @ pos                 # recency evidence for A

    neutral = (np.abs(count) < 1e-9) & (np.abs(rec) > 1e-9)
    if not np.any(neutral):
        return 0.5

    chose_a = resp[neutral] == 0
    fav_a = rec[neutral] > 0      # option supported by the later cues
    followed = np.where(fav_a, chose_a, ~chose_a)
    return float(np.mean(followed))
metric.rationale:
KEY STRUCTURAL FACT: this experiment's validities are all 0.95, so IVC's distrust kernel is constant across features and its subjective weights collapse to EXACTLY flat (w_j = 1/n) for every parameter combination (tau, c, gamma, beta, epsilon all irrelevant). IVC therefore reduces to pure tallying: d = (1/n)*count_diff. On the 16 count-neutral trial types of this design (trials 1,2,5,6,7,8,9,11 and their mirrors; 4 reps each = 64 trials/subject), count_diff = 0, so IVC predicts P = 0.50 exactly, parameter-free, for every subject (the uniform lapse maps 0.5 to 0.5).

SWC cannot be flat: with equal validities vnorm is constant, so w_j = (1-lam)/n + lam*[(1-rho)*0.5 + rho*(j/(n-1))^eta] is strictly increasing in position (lam>=0.8, rho>=0.8). On count-neutral trials its evidence reduces EXACTLY to d = lam*rho * sum_j pos_j * s_j, i.e., a pure recency signal with a strictly positive coefficient. So SWC must prefer the option supported by the later cues on every count-neutral trial, at every point in its parameter box. I verified the corner (lam=0.8, rho=0.8, eta=2.5, beta=0.8): mean recency-following rate ~0.61; mid parameters ~0.70; strong corner (lam=1, rho=1, eta=4.5, beta=1.7) ~0.78. The favored DIRECTION is parameter-free, and the magnitude is bounded away from 0.5 across the entire box.

DELIBERATE EXCLUSIONS: (i) The knife trials 10/22 (four early 95% experts vs the last one) look like an opposite-sign contrast, but SWC's own prediction there flips sign inside its box (at lam=0.8, rho=0.8, eta=2.5 one gets w2+w3+w4+w5 > w6, i.e., SWC follows the majority), so they are unreliable and are excluded by the count-neutrality filter. (ii) Anchor and count-skewed trials (3,4,12,15,16,24) are excluded because both theories agree in direction there and IVC's magnitude is parameter-dependent, which would inject between-subject variance without a clean mean gap.

VARIANCE BUDGET: the metric is a simple binary rate over 64 trials per subject. IVC: every subject sits at exactly 0.50 in expectation, so between-subject variance is pure binomial (~0.25/64 = 0.0039). SWC: binomial (~0.003) plus parameter heterogeneity (~0.002), total ~0.005. Expected mean gap ~0.19 (worst-case SWC corner still 0.10), giving Welch t roughly in the 6-10 range at N=25 -- comfortably below alpha=0.01 in both typical and worst-case regimes. The metric is well-defined on any subject slice (>=1 neutral trial) and on the pooled DataFrame.

proposer_theory.description: INVERTED-VALIDITY COUNTING (IVC) — distrust-weighted tallying. Subjects do read the communicated validities but map them through a systematic distrust inversion: they act as if each stated validity were the expert's error rate, so the most highly validated experts are discounted most. Every discriminating cue is attended deterministically (no attention lapses, no working-memory capacity interference — choice consistency is design-independent). Each cue j carries subjective weight w_j = (1-tau)/n + tau*(1-v_j)^kappa / Z, a mixture of flat counting and a normalized inverted-validity kernel; tau is the trust placed in the inversion, kappa its steepness (kappa=0, tau=0 recovers plain Tallying; large kappa approaches a worst-expert-first one-reason rule). Evidence is integrated additively, d = sum_j w_j * sign(A_j - B_j), and the choice is a logistic function of beta*d plus a small uniform lapse epsilon. Because the anti-validity signature is grounded in the communicated validity values rather than in cue position, it transfers across designs with different validity-position layouts — unlike SWC's recency gradient, which sign-failed the recency-consistency experiment.
proposer_theory.predict_source:
def predict(parameters, state, history):
    # IVC: Inverted-Validity Counting (distrust-weighted tallying),
    # PARTIAL-CENTERING edition, iter-6 kernel-alignment retune.
    # Stimulus: array of shape (2, n_features); row 0 = option A, row 1 = B.
    stim = np.asarray(state, dtype=float)
    if stim.ndim != 2 or stim.shape[0] != 2:
        raise ValueError(
            f"IVC expects a (2, n_features) stimulus; got shape {stim.shape}."
        )
    a, b = stim[0], stim[1]
    n = int(stim.shape[1])

    v = np.asarray(parameters["validities"], dtype=float).ravel()
    if v.shape[0] != n:
        # Graceful fallback: strictly decreasing validities.
        v = np.linspace(0.95, 0.55, n)
    v = np.clip(v, 0.0, 1.0)

    tau = float(parameters["tau"])
    gamma = float(parameters["gamma"])
    c = float(parameters["c"])
    # log-uniform (heavy-tailed) subject-level inverse temperature.
    # Partially retreated to [0.25, 0.70] (beta in [1.8, 5.0], median ~3.0):
    # the iter-5 raise to [0.35, 0.80] fixed the Exp4/Exp7 pair but
    # overshot the moderate-|d| regime (Exp2 contrast and Exp3 coefficient
    # both moved AWAY from target). This is the midpoint between iter-3's
    # [0.15, 0.70] and iter-5's [0.35, 0.80] -- a partial retreat, not a
    # revert -- so the Exp4/Exp7 gains are largely preserved while the
    # spread-error designs (Exp1/2/3/5) recover.
    beta = 10.0 ** float(parameters["log10_beta"])
    eps = float(parameters["epsilon"])

    # (1) PARTIAL distrust inversion. The stated validity is mapped to an
    # error rate (1 - v_j); a FRACTION c of the smallest error rate is
    # subtracted before the gamma power:
    #     inv_j = ((1 - v_j) - c * min_k(1 - v_k))^gamma / Z
    # c = 0 recovers the uncentered kernel; c = 1 is hard centering.
    # c TRIMMED to [0.0, 0.2]: centering steepens the effective kernel;
    # trimming it moves the candidate toward the uncentered kappa=2.7
    # reference kernel that Exp7's metric scores against, and further
    # softens the inversion on the spread-error designs (Exp3/5/8).
    err = 1.0 - v
    centered = np.maximum(err - c * float(err.min()), 0.0)
    inv = np.power(centered, gamma)
    Z = float(inv.sum())
    if Z > 1e-12:
        w_inv = inv / Z
    else:
        # Degenerate design (all validities equal): fall back to flat tally.
        w_inv = np.full(n, 1.0 / n)

    # Subjective weights: mixture of flat counting and the partially
    # centered inverted-validity kernel. tau's lower bound SPLIT to 0.83
    # (midpoint of iter-3's 0.78 and iter-5's 0.88): the 0.88 raise was a
    # suspected co-contributor (with beta) to the Exp3/Exp5/Exp1
    # overshoots, but Exp7 did benefit, so split the difference.
    w = (1.0 - tau) / n + tau * w_inv

    # (2) Deterministic attention: every discriminating cue is always
    # attended. NO capacity interference: beta is design-independent.
    s = np.sign(a - b)

    # (3) Additive integration of all discriminating cues.
    d = float(np.dot(w, s))

    # Numerically stable logistic choice rule.
    p_a = 0.5 * (1.0 + np.tanh(0.5 * beta * d))
    probs = np.array([p_a, 1.0 - p_a], dtype=float)

    # (4) Independent uniform lapse, HELD at [0.08, 0.22]: the beta/eps
    # decoupling from iter-5 is working (Exp4 anchors at 0.8417 vs 0.8433)
    # and must be preserved; if the beta trim drops Exp4 slightly, the
    # lapse continues to carry the anchor cap.
    probs = (1.0 - eps) * probs + eps * 0.5
    return probs
proposer_theory.rationale: This is a minimal, purely parametric edit on the accepted iter-5 base, implementing the critic's iter-6 kernel-alignment diagnosis exactly. The critic's key insight is that the remaining residuals cannot be fixed by noise: Exp2 (+0.160, dominant) and Exp7 (-0.059) read out determinism in OPPOSITE directions through comparable |d| ranges, so the fix must come from the kernel shape. The diagnostic facts: (a) Exp7's metric scores adherence to a FIXED reference kernel (tau=0.925, kappa=2.7, uncentered), and the candidate's median kernel (gamma~3.2 with partial centering) is systematically steeper than that reference — on borderline Exp7 trials the candidate's d flips sign relative to the reference, leaking adherence at fixed noise; (b) gamma acts strongly on the spread-error designs (Exp1/2/3/5, error rates 0.05..0.5) where the 'too inversion-extreme' residuals live, and barely on Exp7's saturated bimodal error structure. EDIT 1: gamma lowered from [2.2, 4.2] to [2.3, 3.2] (median ~2.75, aligned with the kappa=2.7 reference). This raises Exp7 adherence via better sign agreement with the scored kernel WITHOUT another beta raise, while simultaneously softening the inversion on Exps 1/2/3/5 — all currently too extreme — and leaving Exp4 anchors untouched (d = ±1 when all cues agree, so only beta/eps touch anchors). EDIT 2: c trimmed from [0.0, 0.35] to [0.0, 0.2]: centering steepens the effective kernel, so trimming it reinforces the same alignment on Exp7 and further softens the inversion on Exp3/5/8. EDIT 3: log10_beta partially retreated from [0.35, 0.80] to [0.25, 0.70] (median ~3.0) — explicitly the midpoint between iter-3's [0.15, 0.70] and iter-5's [0.35, 0.80], not a revert: Exp2 and Exp3 both moved away from target after the iter-5 beta raise, so some retreat is required, but going below 0.25 would undo the real Exp4/Exp7 gains. EDIT 4: tau's lower bound split from 0.88 to 0.83 (midpoint of 0.78 and 0.88): the 0.88 raise amplified the inverted kernel's share and is a suspected co-contributor (with beta) to the Exp3/Exp5/Exp1 overshoots, but Exp7 did benefit — split the difference rather than full revert. HELD: epsilon at [0.08, 0.22] per the critic's explicit instruction to preserve the working beta/eps decoupling (Exp4 anchors landed at 0.8417 vs 0.8433 — essentially perfect); per-subject sampling scheme unchanged; per-cue bias term still omitted. Expectation management per the critic: Exp2 has never landed below 0.233 in any IVC configuration across five iterations, so it will likely land ~0.22-0.25 rather than 0.158 — that ~+0.07 is accepted as the in-family floor and NOT chased with noise increases that would re-break the Exp4/Exp7 pair. Projected landing: Exp1 ~0.19, Exp2 ~0.24, Exp3 ~-0.60, Exp4 ~0.84, Exp5 ~0.21, Exp6 ~0.40, Exp7 ~0.75-0.78, Exp8 ~0.35 — a net loss clearly below the 0.1047 floor, with no experiment materially worse than iter-5's residuals and five of eight improving.

experiment.rationale:
STRUCTURAL LEVER. IVC's weights are a function of validity VALUES ONLY (distrust kernel (1-v)^gamma), with zero position sensitivity; SWC's weights are dominated by POSITION (convex recency, lam*rho >= 0.64) with only a weak min-max validity component (<= 0.20). Prior IVC-vs-SWC designs used non-monotone duplicated validities [6], a strictly increasing ladder [7], or a single worst expert [8]. This design uses an untried PALINDROMIC validity profile v = [0.55, 0.95, 0.75, 0.75, 0.95, 0.55] (n=6). Because IVC's weights depend only on validity values, its weight profile is exactly POSITION-SYMMETRIC (w1 = w6, w2 = w5, w3 = w4), while SWC's is strictly position-graded and late-heavy. The palindrome therefore creates validity-MATCHED comparisons at every position separation, pinning IVC to exact, parameter-free point predictions that SWC's recency gradient must break. All boxes below were verified at the corners of both parameter spaces (SWC's eta corners 2.5/4.5 with lam*rho in [0.64, 1]; IVC's gamma/tau/c/beta/eps corners).

AXIS 1 - VALIDITY-MATCHED RECENCY LADDER (R1, R2, R3 + mirrors). Duels between validity-equal experts at maximal (e1 vs e6, both 55%), large (e2 vs e5, both 95%), and minimal (e3 vs e4, both 75%) position separation. IVC: d = 0 EXACTLY for every parameter combination -> P(A) = 0.50 parameter-free (the uniform lapse preserves 0.5). SWC: d = -lam*rho*(1 - (k/5)^eta-differences), giving P(A) boxes [0.15, 0.38] (R1), [0.28, 0.45] (R2), [0.42, 0.49] (R3). SWC REQUIRES a monotone ladder with within-subject spread P(R3) - P(R1) in [0.10, 0.32] (the ratio |d_R1|/|d_R3| >= 5.6 at every corner); IVC requires exactly 0 on all three. Observed P(later expert's product) > 0.55 on R1 is impossible for IVC at ANY admissible parameter combination and required by SWC.

AXIS 2 - VALIDITY-MATCHED COALITIONS (K1-K5, D4 + mirrors; 12 of 32 trials). Coalitions whose validity multisets match exactly (K1: {0.55,0.95} vs {0.55,0.95}; K2: {0.55,0.75} both; K3: {0.95,0.75} both; K4: {0.55,0.95,0.75} both; K5: {0.55,0.75} both; D4: interleaved {0.55,0.75,0.95} both). IVC predicts EXACTLY 0.50 on all twelve, parameter-free. SWC's recency gradient requires late-block preference with boxes P(A) in [0.07, 0.40] (K1), [0.12, 0.37] (K2), [0.22, 0.45] (K3), [0.05, 0.33] (K4 - the half-block flip, the headline trial), [0.17, 0.40] (K5), [0.23, 0.42] (D4). Any reliable deviation from 0.50 in the late direction on this family falsifies IVC's entire parameter space; flatness at 0.50 falsifies SWC's.

AXIS 3 - POSITION-TRANSFER PAIRS (T1a/T1b, T2a/T2b + mirrors). Same validity allegiance, opposite position allegiance. T1a: A wins the 55% expert at position 1 vs B wins the 75% expert at position 3; T1b: A wins the 55% expert at position 6 vs B wins the 75% expert at position 4. IVC: d = w(0.55) - w(0.75) on BOTH -> IDENTICAL predictions P(A) in [0.58, 0.84] on the pair. SWC: P(T1a) in [0.42, 0.50] (early low-validity cue loses to a mid cue) but P(T1b) in [0.65, 0.83] (the same low-validity cue, placed last, beats the mid cue) - a REQUIRED pair difference >= 0.15 where IVC requires exactly 0. T1a alone is also a sign dissociation: IVC > 0.58, SWC < 0.50. T2a/T2b repeat the logic with the 95% vs 75% experts (positions 2 vs 4, and 5 vs 3): IVC identical [0.40, 0.48] on both; SWC [0.47, 0.49] vs [0.57, 0.70], required spread >= 0.08. Any within-family difference kills IVC's position-invariance; flatness within families kills SWC's recency gradient.

AXIS 4 - IVC-DIAGNOSTIC CELLS (D1, D2 + mirrors; deliberately adversarial, two-sided design). D1: the 55% expert at position 1 vs the 95% expert at position 2. IVC's distrust inversion predicts subjects prefer the WORSE expert's product: P(A) in [0.63, 0.81]; SWC predicts [0.44, 0.50] (non-overlapping). D2 (worst-expert veto): the lone 55% first expert against FOUR better experts (95/75/75/95). IVC: P(55%-expert's product) in [0.52, 0.80]; SWC: [0.09, 0.41] (non-overlapping). Observed preference for the 55% expert beyond 0.50 on D1/D2 falsifies SWC's entire space - these cells make the design genuinely risky for the advocated theory rather than one-sided.

AXIS 5 - ANCHOR (TOT + mirror). Total split: both theories predict >= 0.69, establishing task comprehension and overall responsiveness.

PARAMETRIC SIGNATURE. IVC predicts only ~6 distinct probability levels across all 32 pairs (exactly 0.50 on the 18 validity-matched trials; one level per validity-allegation multiset on the transfer/duel trials; high confidence on TOT), with EXACT equalities within families. SWC predicts a position-ordered profile breaking every equality. Regressing P(A) on recency evidence sum((j/5)^3.5 * s_j) versus inverted-validity evidence sum((1-v_j)^2.7 * s_j) yields opposite-loading profiles: the two axes are decorrelated by the palindrome (expert 1: high inverted weight, zero recency; expert 6: equally high inverted weight, maximal recency - the transfer pairs exploit exactly this). Every conflict type appears in A/B-mirrored form to absorb side and position bias. 32 unique pairs, K = 96 // 32 = 3 repetitions in independently randomized order = exactly 96 trials per subject.

metric.metric_source:
def metric(data: pd.DataFrame) -> float:
    # Recency-gradient choice score on theory-divergent trials.
    #
    # Design validities: experts at positions 1 and 4 (0-indexed 0 and 3)
    # have validity 0.95; the other four experts have validity 0.75.
    #
    # Per trial:
    #   s_j = sign(A_j - B_j)   which option expert j favors
    #   x   = sum_j p_j * s_j   recency evidence for A, with convex
    #                           position weights p_j = (j/5)^3.5
    #   y   = +1 if A chosen, -1 if B chosen
    #
    # Scored trial families (48 of the 96 trials per subject):
    # (1) VALIDITY-MATCHED trials (types 3/4, 9/10, 13/14, 17/18, 25/26
    #     plus mirrors): the two options' discriminating experts carry
    #     identical validity multisets. Any validity-only weighting (IVC)
    #     yields exactly zero evidence, so E[x*y] = 0 for EVERY parameter
    #     combination (the uniform lapse preserves 0.5). SWC's convex
    #     recency gradient makes E[x*y] strongly positive.
    # (2) VALIDITY-CONFOUNDED trials (types 5/6, 11/12, 23/24 plus
    #     mirrors): the option whose experts sit LATER also carries
    #     strictly more 0.95 experts. IVC's distrust inversion favors
    #     the EARLY option, so E[x*y] < 0; SWC's recency gradient still
    #     favors the LATE option, so E[x*y] > 0.
    #
    # Metric = mean of x*y over these trials.
    # SWC: strongly positive (~ +0.28 across its box, range ~ +0.17..+0.41).
    # IVC: zero on the matched family for all parameters, slightly
    # negative overall (~ -0.03).

    n = 6
    V = np.array([0.95, 0.75, 0.75, 0.95, 0.75, 0.75])
    P = (np.arange(n, dtype=float) / float(n - 1)) ** 3.5
    hi = V >= 0.9

    def to_arr(cell):
        if isinstance(cell, np.ndarray):
            return np.asarray(cell, dtype=float).ravel()
        if isinstance(cell, (list, tuple)):
            return np.asarray(list(cell), dtype=float).ravel()
        txt = str(cell).strip().strip('[]()')
        parts = txt.replace(',', ' ').split()
        return np.asarray([float(t) for t in parts], dtype=float).ravel()

    a_cells = data['option_a_ratings'].tolist()
    b_cells = data['option_b_ratings'].tolist()
    r_cells = data['response'].tolist()

    scores = []
    for i in range(len(a_cells)):
        try:
            a = to_arr(a_cells[i])
            b = to_arr(b_cells[i])
        except Exception:
            continue
        if a.shape[0] != n or b.shape[0] != n:
            continue
        try:
            resp = int(r_cells[i])
        except Exception:
            continue
        if resp != 0 and resp != 1:
            continue

        s = np.sign(a - b)
        ia = np.where(s > 0)[0]
        ib = np.where(s < 0)[0]
        if ia.size == 0 or ib.size == 0:
            continue

        va = sorted(V[ia].tolist())
        vb = sorted(V[ib].tolist())
        matched = (va == vb)

        x = float(np.dot(P, s))
        if not matched:
            if x == 0:
                continue
            late_a = x > 0
            late_hi = int(hi[ia].sum()) if late_a else int(hi[ib].sum())
            early_hi = int(hi[ib].sum()) if late_a else int(hi[ia].sum())
            if late_hi <= early_hi:
                continue

        y = 1.0 if resp == 0 else -1.0
        scores.append(x * y)

    if len(scores) == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(np.mean(scores))
metric.rationale: This metric estimates the CHOICE-RECENCY GRADIENT as a continuous covariance-style score, qualitatively different from the previously attempted binary later-option rate: instead of collapsing each trial to 'did the subject pick the later option', it weights each choice by the graded recency imbalance x = sum_j (j/5)^3.5 * sign(A_j - B_j), so trials with large position separation (the half-block flip, the 2-vs-6-cue coalitions) dominate the estimate, which both enlarges the between-theory mean gap and matches SWC's convex gradient shape. Trial selection is purely structural: (a) all trials whose two options' discriminating experts have identical validity multisets (types 3/4, 9/10, 13/14, 17/18, 25/26 with mirrors; 30 trials/subject), where IVC's validity-only weights give d = 0 exactly for every parameter combination (the uniform lapse preserves P = 0.5), so E[x*y] = 0 parameter-free, while SWC's rho*(j/5)^eta recency term (rho >= 0.8) forces a positive score; and (b) trials where the later-cue option carries strictly MORE 0.95 experts (types 5/6, 11/12, 23/24 with mirrors; 18 trials/subject), where IVC's distrust inversion favors the EARLY low-validity side (E[x*y] < 0) and SWC still favors the LATE side (E[x*y] > 0). Verified at central parameters: IVC mean = -0.03 (exactly 0 on the matched family, mildly negative on the confounded family), SWC mean = +0.28, with SWC's value staying in [+0.17, +0.41] across all corners of its box (lam, rho, eta, beta, eps) and IVC's staying in [-0.06, -0.01] across its box — the intervals never overlap. Per-subject standard deviation is ~0.11 for both theories (binomial choice noise over 48 scored trials plus modest parameter spread; the score is bounded by |x| <= 1.58), so at N = 25 the Welch t on (point_estimate, between_subject_variance) is expected around 8-10, far below alpha = 0.01. Every scored trial type appears in A/B-mirrored form, so pure side biases cancel; the anchor and all trials where the two theories agree in direction are excluded so they cannot dilute the contrast. A value near 0 or negative falsifies SWC's recency gradient; a reliably positive value (above ~ +0.1) is impossible for IVC at any admissible parameter combination.

proposer_theory.description: Subjective-Weighted Counting with convex cue-order recency (SWC), deterministic-attention variant. People integrate ALL discriminating cues additively with no capacity interference, but the cue weights are subjective and only partially calibrated to communicated validities: w_j = (1-lambda)/n + lambda*[(1-rho)*vnorm_j + rho*(j/(n-1))^eta]. Because validities are always presented in strictly decreasing feature order, the convex recency gradient is anti-correlated with validity, producing within-margin anti-validity preferences (Experiment 3's negative d-coefficient) while preserving mostly-tally aggregate behavior. Attention to cues is deterministic (every cue is always attended); the only stochasticity is the logistic choice noise itself plus a small uniform lapse epsilon. This edition implements the critic's in-family tuning: the noise channels that let the fit collapse to flat counting are removed or tightened so the recency gradient must do the work.
proposer_theory.predict_source:
def predict(parameters, state, history):
    # SWC: Subjective-Weighted Counting with convex cue-order recency
    # (deterministic-attention variant).
    # Stimulus: array of shape (2, n_features); row 0 = option A, row 1 = B.
    stim = np.asarray(state, dtype=float)
    if stim.ndim != 2 or stim.shape[0] != 2:
        raise ValueError(
            f"SWC expects a (2, n_features) stimulus; got shape {stim.shape}."
        )
    a, b = stim[0], stim[1]
    n = int(stim.shape[1])

    v = np.asarray(parameters["validities"], dtype=float).ravel()
    if v.shape[0] != n:
        # Graceful fallback: linearly decreasing validities.
        v = np.linspace(0.95, 0.55, n)

    lam = float(parameters["lambda"])
    rho = float(parameters["rho"])
    eta = float(parameters["eta"])
    beta = float(parameters["beta"])
    eps = float(parameters["epsilon"])

    # (1) Subjective validity component: min-max normalized validities.
    vspan = float(v.max() - v.min())
    if vspan > 1e-12:
        vnorm = (v - v.min()) / vspan
    else:
        vnorm = np.full(n, 0.5)

    # (2) Recency component: position in presentation order, convexly
    # transformed so that late cues can be strongly overweighted.
    if n > 1:
        pos = (np.arange(n, dtype=float) / (n - 1.0)) ** eta
    else:
        pos = np.full(n, 0.5)

    # Subjective weights: mixture of flat counting, validity-following,
    # and recency-following. Because validities are presented in strictly
    # decreasing feature order, the recency part is anti-correlated with
    # validity -- the source of within-margin anti-validity preferences.
    g = (1.0 - rho) * vnorm + rho * pos
    w = (1.0 - lam) / n + lam * g

    # (3) Deterministic attention: every cue is attended on every trial
    # (per-cue attention lapse removed -- real subjects are highly
    # consistent, and stochastic lapses were the dominant noise source
    # inflating between-subject variance).
    s = np.sign(a - b)

    # Additive integration of all discriminating cues.
    # NO capacity interference: beta is design-independent.
    d = float(np.sum(w * s))

    # Numerically stable logistic.
    p_a = 0.5 * (1.0 + np.tanh(0.5 * beta * d))
    probs = np.array([p_a, 1.0 - p_a], dtype=float)

    # (4) Independent uniform lapse.
    probs = (1.0 - eps) * probs + eps * 0.5
    return probs
proposer_theory.rationale: Minimal-diff edit of the accepted SWC base, applying the critic's four in-family prescriptions. (1) CUT THE NOISE: the per-cue stochastic attention (alpha drawn per trial) was removed entirely — every cue is now always attended. This was the dominant variance source behind Experiment 3's between-subject variance of 0.2046 (real: 0.0186): binomial per-cue dropout made single subjects wildly inconsistent and let the fit soften aggregate rates with noise instead of using the recency gradient. The uniform lapse epsilon is retained but tightened to [0, 0.03]. (2) FORCE THE RECENCY GRADIENT TO ENGAGE: lambda is now [0.8, 1.0], rho [0.8, 1.0], eta [2.5, 4.5], so the flat-counting collapse (lambda ~ 0) that produced Exp 3 ~ 0 is unreachable; the mixture is always dominated by the graded (validity + convex recency) component. (3) MODERATE BETA: beta is capped at 1.7 (previous range went to 8), so conflict probabilities stay in the 0.6-0.9 band rather than saturating — this is what Experiment 2's near-indifferent contrast (real 0.158) requires. (4) ANCHORS: with no interference and moderate beta, hand computation at the range midpoint (lambda~0.9, rho~0.9, eta~3.5, beta~1.2) gives: Exp 4 anchor allegiance ~0.83 (real 0.843) — the 7-1 anchors with the loss on the last cue land near p~0.65, cooling the previous 0.900; Exp 1 TTB-adherence ~0.21 (real 0.208); Exp 2 contrast ~0.19-0.21 (real 0.158, down from 0.321); Exp 3 partial d-coefficient ~ -0.4 at the midpoint and ~ -0.55 to -0.68 at the recency-heavy corner (rho -> 1, lambda -> 1, beta ~1.2-1.3), bracketing the real -0.5756 — a massive improvement over the previous +0.026. The convex recency term is preserved unchanged: it remains the only in-family degree of freedom that yields Experiment 3's negative within-margin coefficient while keeping Experiments 1, 2 and 4 near their targets, and the tightened ranges now force the fit into that basin instead of the noise-dominated flat-counting region the previous parameterization permitted.

next_theory.description: PRIMACY-WEIGHTED INVERTED-VALIDITY COUNTING (PW-IVC). Subjects read the communicated validities but systematically distrust-invert them: they act as if each stated validity were the expert's error rate, so highly validated experts are discounted most (the anti-validity signature). Independently and additively, subjective attention is tilted toward EARLY-presented cues by a steep convex primacy gradient concentrated on the first one or two positions, at a small-to-moderate share of the subjective-weight mixture so the distrust kernel retains dominance wherever validity information varies. Each cue j carries weight w_j = (1-tau)/n + tau * [ (1-rho) * ((1-v_j) - c*min_k(1-v_k))^gamma / Z_v + rho * ((n-j)/(n-1))^eta / Z_p ]; evidence d = sum_j w_j * sign(A_j - B_j) is integrated additively over all discriminating cues; choice is logistic in beta*d with a small uniform lapse epsilon. On tied-validity designs the distrust kernel is exactly flat and the primacy kernel alone supplies the early-vs-late contrast, producing below-chance recency-following; on decreasing-validity layouts the distrust kernel dominates and reproduces the anti-validity regression signature.
next_theory.predict_source:
def predict(parameters, state, history):
    # PW-IVC: Primacy-Weighted Inverted-Validity Counting.
    # iter-4 minimal-diff edit per critic's iter-3 directive:
    #   (1) rho ceiling trimmed 0.34 -> 0.30 (restores distrust dominance in
    #       strictly-decreasing-validity layouts; the iter-3 ceiling raise is
    #       what regressed Exp3 from -0.434 to -0.372);
    #   (2) beta ceiling raised 6.5 -> 8.0 and epsilon floor lowered
    #       0.08 -> 0.06 (the commitment knobs that compensate the
    #       tied-validity experiments for the rho trim and de-attenuate the
    #       Exp3 OLS coefficient);
    #   (3) everything else frozen (tau, eta, gamma, c).
    # Mechanism structure unchanged from the accepted iter-3 base.
    # Stimulus: array of shape (2, n_features); row 0 = option A, row 1 = B.
    stim = np.asarray(state, dtype=float)
    if stim.ndim != 2 or stim.shape[0] != 2:
        raise ValueError(
            f"PW-IVC expects a (2, n_features) stimulus; got shape {stim.shape}."
        )
    a, b = stim[0], stim[1]
    n = int(stim.shape[1])

    v = np.asarray(parameters["validities"], dtype=float).ravel()
    if v.shape[0] != n:
        # Graceful fallback: strictly decreasing validities.
        v = np.linspace(0.95, 0.55, n)
    v = np.clip(v, 0.0, 1.0)

    tau = float(parameters["tau"])      # trust in the non-flat kernel mixture
    rho = float(parameters["rho"])        # primacy share within the mixture
    eta = float(parameters["eta"])       # convexity of the primacy gradient
    gamma = float(parameters["gamma"])   # steepness of distrust inversion
    c = float(parameters["c"])           # partial centering of error rates
    beta = float(parameters["beta"])
    eps = float(parameters["epsilon"])

    # (1) DISTRUST INVERSION with partial centering: treat the stated
    # validity as an error rate; subtract a fraction c of the smallest
    # error rate before raising to the gamma power, then normalize.
    #     inv_j = ((1 - v_j) - c * min_k(1 - v_k))^gamma / Z_v
    # When all validities are tied this kernel is flat (or degenerate at
    # c -> 1, where we fall back to flat), so tied-validity designs are
    # carried entirely by the primacy kernel below.
    err = 1.0 - v
    centered = np.maximum(err - c * float(err.min()), 0.0)
    inv = np.power(centered, gamma)
    Z_v = float(inv.sum())
    if Z_v > 1e-12:
        w_inv = inv / Z_v
    else:
        w_inv = np.full(n, 1.0 / n)

    # (2) STEEP CONVEX PRIMACY GRADIENT over presentation positions: cue j
    # gets raw primacy mass ((n - j)/(n - 1))^eta with eta >= 3.5, so the
    # gradient is concentrated on the FIRST one or two positions. This
    # maximizes the early-vs-late weight CONTRAST per unit of mixture
    # share rho (what the anti-recency metrics score), while the small-to-
    # moderate rho keeps the primacy kernel from fighting the distrust
    # kernel on decreasing-validity layouts (Exps 3, 5, 8).
    if n > 1:
        pos = np.arange(n, dtype=float)
        prim = np.power((n - pos) / (n - 1.0), eta)
    else:
        prim = np.ones(1)
    Z_p = float(prim.sum())
    w_prim = prim / Z_p

    # (3) Subjective weights: mixture of flat counting, the partially
    # centered inverted-validity kernel, and the primacy kernel.
    # tau ~ 0.9+ keeps the non-flat kernels dominant; rho <= 0.30 keeps
    # the distrust kernel the dominant carrier of validity variance.
    w = (1.0 - tau) / n + tau * ((1.0 - rho) * w_inv + rho * w_prim)

    # (4) Deterministic attention: every discriminating cue is always
    # attended; no capacity interference, beta is design-independent.
    s = np.sign(a - b)

    # (5) Additive integration of all discriminating cues.
    d = float(np.dot(w, s))

    # Numerically stable logistic choice rule.
    p_a = 0.5 * (1.0 + np.tanh(0.5 * beta * d))
    probs = np.array([p_a, 1.0 - p_a], dtype=float)

    # (6) Small independent uniform lapse, capping anchor adherence.
    probs = (1.0 - eps) * probs + eps * 0.5
    return probs
next_theory.rationale: Minimal-diff edit exactly per the critic's iter-3 directive; the PW-IVC mechanism and all code are unchanged from the accepted iter-3 base, and only three parameter-box knobs move. (1) rho: [0.16, 0.34] -> [0.16, 0.30]. The iter-3 ceiling raise is what regressed Exp3 from -0.434 to -0.372 (squared error ~0.042, now the dominant loss term): in the strictly-decreasing-validity layout, primacy mass (pro-early = pro-high-validity) directly cancels the distrust kernel, and the fitter was buying Exp9/Exp10 gains with primacy mass at Exp3's expense. The modest ceiling trim — placed between iter-2's 0.28 and iter-3's 0.34, not back at either, to avoid the oscillation the critic warns about — restores distrust dominance in decreasing-validity layouts. (2) beta: [2.2, 6.5] -> [2.2, 8.0], and epsilon floor: 0.08 -> 0.06. These are the commitment knobs that COMPENSATE the tied-validity experiments for the rho trim: on Exp9's count-neutral trials the anti-recency deviation from 0.5 scales roughly with beta*rho at small evidence, so a ~12% rho cut is offset by the ~23% beta headroom, while on Exps 3/5/7/10 the distrust evidence already points the right way and sharper commitment pushes each under-signed metric toward its target (Exp3 more negative toward -0.576, Exp5 toward 0.231, Exp7 up toward 0.788, Exp10 toward -0.173). The lower epsilon floor additionally de-attenuates the Exp3 OLS coefficient, which the lapse shrinks toward zero by roughly (1-eps). (3) Everything else frozen: tau [0.88, 0.97], eta [3.5, 6.5], gamma [2.9, 3.8], c [0.0, 0.2] — all worked in both prior accepted iterations. Guardrails per the critic: Exp4's anchor is lapse-capped (adherence ~ 1 - eps/2 at saturation, so the lowered epsilon floor could push it up — the ceiling 0.22 keeps the mean near 0.84, and if Exp4 exceeds 0.88 the epsilon floor should be restored to 0.10 rather than capping beta); Exp8 is accepted as the family residual (all distrust-flavored theories undershoot the real 0.396) and is monitored but not purchased at the cost of the signature experiments; Exp2 (currently +0.055) is monitored — higher beta sharpens its tally-vs-TTB contrast in the wrong direction, but the signature experiments (3, 5, 7, 9, 10) take priority, exactly as directed. The iter-1 -> iter-3 trajectory (Exp3 error +0.51 -> +0.14 -> +0.20, aggregate 0.151 -> 0.101 -> 0.099) confirms the structure is right; this final coordinated nudge on commitment level and the rho ceiling targets a loss below the 0.0989 floor.

experiment.rationale:
STRUCTURAL LEVER. IVC and PW-IVC share the distrust-inversion kernel; they differ ONLY in that PW-IVC adds a convex primacy gradient concentrated on the first one or two positions (mixture share tau*rho in [0.14, 0.29]; positions 1-2 carry ~82-94% of the primacy kernel, and position 1 alone carries 0.53-0.72). IVC's weights are a function of validity VALUES ONLY -- strictly position-invariant. The design therefore manipulates POSITION while holding validity allegiances fixed, using the layout v = [0.95, 0.60, 0.60, 0.95, 0.60, 0.95], which (i) decorrelates validity from position (three 0.60 experts at positions 2,3,5; three 0.95 experts at positions 1,4,6), (ii) places a 0.95 expert at POSITION 1 -- the maximal-primacy slot carrying ~0.1% of IVC's kernel mass -- creating head-to-head primacy-vs-distrust conflicts, and (iii) triplicates each validity level, enabling validity-matched cells where IVC is pinned to exact point predictions. Because (0.40/0.05)^gamma is ~125-340, the three 0.60 experts absorb ~99.8% of the distrust kernel: every 0.60-vs-0.95 allegiance imbalance moves d by ~tau*(1/3) regardless of which positions are involved. All boxes below were verified at the corners of both parameter spaces, respecting the coupling between the kernel coefficient tau*(1-rho) and the primacy coefficient tau*rho.

AXIS 1 -- VALIDITY-MATCHED PRIMACY DOSE LADDER (trials 1-14). Duels and coalitions whose validity multisets match exactly (e.g., A wins the 0.95 expert at position 1 vs B the 0.95 expert at position 6; A wins {0.95@1, 0.60@2} vs B {0.60@5, 0.95@6}). IVC: d = 0 EXACTLY for every parameter combination -> P = 0.500 parameter-free on ALL 14 matched cells. PW-IVC: d = tau*rho*(primacy contrast) > 0 strictly, growing with position contrast: near-zero dose D3 (positions 4 vs 6) P in [0.50, 0.52]; low doses (0.60-duels, positions 2v3, 3v5, 2v5) P in [0.50, 0.63]; high dose D1 (position 1 vs 6) P in [0.53, 0.82]; max dose C1 ({1,2} vs {5,6}) P in [0.55, 0.86]. Observed preference >= 0.55 for the earlier expert's product on the D1/C1 family is impossible for IVC at ANY admissible parameter combination; flat 0.500 across the ladder falsifies PW-IVC. The slope of P versus primacy contrast is EXACTLY 0 under IVC and strictly positive under PW-IVC -- a parametric signature.

AXIS 2 -- FIVE-WAY EXACT EQUALITY (T1a/T1b/T1c/M7a/M7b + mirrors; trials 15-20, 25-28). All five hold validity allegiances fixed (T1: A wins one 0.60 vs B one 0.95; M7: A wins two 0.60 + one 0.95 vs B one 0.60 + two 0.95) while permuting positions, so d_IVC = tau*(w60 - w95) IDENTICALLY: IVC predicts ONE probability, box [0.59, 0.81], on all TEN cells. PW-IVC predicts a strict ordering for every admissible parameter set: M7a (A's wins at positions 1-3) [0.65, 0.91] > T1b (0.60@2 vs 0.95@6) [0.57, 0.90] > T1c (0.60@3 vs 0.95@4) [0.53, 0.87] > T1a (0.60@5 vs 0.95@1) [0.50, 0.79] > M7b (A's wins at 3,5,6 vs B's at 1,2,4) [0.44, 0.77]. On M7b PW-IVC's box dips BELOW CHANCE on the very allegiance pattern where it predicts 0.65-0.91 when positions are permuted, while IVC requires the same probability. Any reliable spread across the family (or a sub-0.5 proportion on M7b) kills IVC; equality kills PW-IVC.

AXIS 3 -- 2v2 TRANSFER (trials 21-24). A wins both 0.60s, B both 0.95s, positions permuted (A@{2,3} vs B@{4,6} vs A@{3,5} vs B@{1,4}). IVC: identical [0.68, 0.93] on all four cells. PW-IVC: T2a [0.75, 0.92] vs T2b [0.59, 0.89] with a pointwise strict ordering -- a required spread where IVC requires exactly 0.

AXIS 4 -- PRIMACY-RESCUE (trials 31-32). The product endorsed by the three 95% experts (positions 1, 4, 6) vs the product endorsed by a single 60% expert (position 5). IVC: the worst-expert veto, P(60%-product) in [0.57, 0.81]. PW-IVC: position-1 primacy (0.53-0.72 of the primacy kernel) fights the distrust kernel, d in [-0.03, +0.17], P in [0.42, 0.78] with sub-chance values at strong-primacy corners -- a confidence dilution (and possible sign reversal) IVC cannot produce anywhere in its box.

AXIS 5 -- SHARED-CORE ANCHOR AND NULL CONTROL (trials 29-30; trial 3-4). E2: the three 60% experts' product vs the three 95% experts' product at a 3-3 count tie: both theories confidently favor the 60% product (IVC [0.74, 0.95], PW [0.71, 0.97]) -- verifying that subjects read and distrust-invert the communicated validities (and screening out plain tallying, which predicts exactly 0.5). D3 (0.95@4 vs 0.95@6) is the zero-dose rung: both theories ~0.5, assaying generic side/late-position bias.

PARAMETRIC SIGNATURE. IVC predicts only FIVE distinct probability levels across all 32 pairs (exactly 0.500 on the 14 matched cells; one level on the ten T1/M7 cells; one on the four T2 cells; one on E2; one on V1; mirrors give complements), with EXACT equalities within families. PW-IVC predicts a position-graded profile that breaks every equality in a parameter-free direction. Regressing P(A) on primacy evidence (position-gradient-weighted cue signs, e.g., eta=5) controlling for inverted-validity evidence yields a primacy coefficient of exactly 0 under IVC and strictly positive under PW-IVC. 32 unique pairs, K = 96 // 32 = 3 repetitions in independently randomized order = exactly 96 trials; every cell appears in A/B-mirrored form (16 complement pairs) to absorb side bias.

metric.metric_source:
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

def metric(data: pd.DataFrame) -> float:
    # Within-allegiance-cell OLS slope of choice on reference primacy evidence.
    #
    # Identification: group every trial by (c1, c2) where
    #   c1 = number of 0.60-expert wins for A minus for B (positions 2,3,5),
    #   c2 = total signed cue count.
    # Any position-INVARIANT validity-weighted model (IVC at ANY parameter
    # combo, plain tallying, any lapse/transform) makes P(choose A) a function
    # of (c1, c2) ONLY. Demeaning the primacy regressor within these cells
    # therefore makes the population OLS slope EXACTLY 0 under IVC,
    # parameter-free, for every subject. PW-IVC's primacy gradient breaks the
    # cell-conditional independence, producing a strictly positive slope.

    ratings_a = data['option_a_ratings']
    ratings_b = data['option_b_ratings']
    A = np.array([np.asarray(r, dtype=float) for r in ratings_a], dtype=float)
    B = np.array([np.asarray(r, dtype=float) for r in ratings_b], dtype=float)
    if A.ndim != 2 or A.shape[0] == 0:
        return 0.0
    n = A.shape[1]

    # Reference primacy kernel, eta = 5 (middle of PW-IVC's eta range [3.5, 6.5]).
    if n > 1:
        pos = np.arange(n, dtype=float)
        wp = ((n - pos) / (n - 1.0)) ** 5.0
        wp = wp / wp.sum()
    else:
        wp = np.ones(1)

    S = np.sign(A - B)
    y = 1.0 - np.asarray(data['response'], dtype=float)  # 1 = chose A

    x1 = S.dot(wp)  # primacy evidence favoring A

    # Allegiance cell for this design: validities [0.95, 0.6, 0.6, 0.95, 0.6, 0.95]
    # -> 0.60 experts at 0-indexed positions 1, 2, 4.
    if n == 6:
        c1 = S[:, 1] + S[:, 2] + S[:, 4]
    else:
        c1 = np.zeros(A.shape[0])
    c2 = S.sum(axis=1)

    g = c1.astype(int).astype(str) + "_" + c2.astype(int).astype(str)
    df = pd.DataFrame({'x1': x1, 'y': y, 'g': g})

    # Demean primacy evidence within allegiance cell: removes ALL validity-based
    # mean structure (distrust kernel at any gamma/c/tau, flat counting, lapse).
    df['x1c'] = df['x1'] - df.groupby('g')['x1'].transform('mean')
    ssx = float((df['x1c'] ** 2).sum())
    if ssx <= 1e-12:
        return 0.0
    ybar = float(df['y'].mean())
    slope = float((df['x1c'] * (df['y'] - ybar)).sum() / ssx)
    return slope
metric.rationale: PRIMACY SLOPE AT FIXED VALIDITY ALLEGIANCE. The two theories share the distrust-inversion kernel and differ ONLY in the position-dependent primacy component, so the metric must isolate position effects while absorbing all validity-based structure. Key algebraic fact: for ANY position-invariant weight vector w (IVC at any tau/gamma/c, plain tallying, plus any lapse), the latent evidence is w·s = (w60−w95)·c1 + w95·c2, where c1 = (s2+s3+s5) is the 0.60-expert allegiance count and c2 = total signed cue count. Hence P(choose A) is a function of the cell (c1, c2) alone. The metric groups trials by (c1, c2) (9 non-empty cells in this design: the 14 validity-matched pairs form cell (0,0); the T1/M7 family forms (±1,0); T2 forms (±2,0); E2 forms (±3,0); V1 forms (∓1,±2)), demeans a fixed reference primacy kernel score x1 = w_prim·s (eta=5, the midpoint of PW-IVC's eta range, so the kernel mismatch attenuation is <2% at both eta corners) within cell, and returns the OLS slope of choice on the demeaned score. Because the within-cell sum of the demeaned regressor is exactly zero, the population slope is EXACTLY 0 under IVC for every admissible parameter combination — the per-subject distribution under IVC is pure binomial noise (SD ≈ 0.11 from ~0.22 residual variance over Σx̃² ≈ 18.2 across 96 trials), with no parameter heterogeneity contribution. Under PW-IVC the slope is strictly positive at every parameter point: within-cell position contrasts (e.g., M7a x1=+0.93 vs M7b x1=−0.72 inside cell (1,0); the matched-cell dose ladder inside cell (0,0); T2a vs T2b inside cell (2,0)) all push choices toward the earlier-position option. Corner calculations give slopes ≈ 0.05 (beta=2.2, rho=0.16), ≈ 0.15 (mid-range), ≈ 0.30 (beta=8, rho=0.30), i.e., mean ≈ 0.14–0.15 with between-subject SD ≈ 0.12 (binomial + parameter spread). At N=25 the Welch t-statistic is ≈ 4+ (p ≈ 1e-4), comfortably below alpha=0.01, with the IVC side pinned at zero variance-inflating structure. The metric works identically on the pooled DataFrame and on single-subject slices (each subject sees all 32 pairs × 3 reps, so cells are identically composed).

proposer_theory.description: INVERTED-VALIDITY COUNTING (IVC) — distrust-weighted tallying. Subjects do read the communicated validities but map them through a systematic distrust inversion: they act as if each stated validity were the expert's error rate, so the most highly validated experts are discounted most. Every discriminating cue is attended deterministically (no attention lapses, no working-memory capacity interference — choice consistency is design-independent). Each cue j carries subjective weight w_j = (1-tau)/n + tau*(1-v_j)^kappa / Z, a mixture of flat counting and a normalized inverted-validity kernel; tau is the trust placed in the inversion, kappa its steepness (kappa=0, tau=0 recovers plain Tallying; large kappa approaches a worst-expert-first one-reason rule). Evidence is integrated additively, d = sum_j w_j * sign(A_j - B_j), and the choice is a logistic function of beta*d plus a small uniform lapse epsilon. Because the anti-validity signature is grounded in the communicated validity values rather than in cue position, it transfers across designs with different validity-position layouts — unlike SWC's recency gradient, which sign-failed the recency-consistency experiment.
proposer_theory.predict_source:
def predict(parameters, state, history):
    # IVC: Inverted-Validity Counting (distrust-weighted tallying),
    # PARTIAL-CENTERING edition, iter-6 kernel-alignment retune.
    # Stimulus: array of shape (2, n_features); row 0 = option A, row 1 = B.
    stim = np.asarray(state, dtype=float)
    if stim.ndim != 2 or stim.shape[0] != 2:
        raise ValueError(
            f"IVC expects a (2, n_features) stimulus; got shape {stim.shape}."
        )
    a, b = stim[0], stim[1]
    n = int(stim.shape[1])

    v = np.asarray(parameters["validities"], dtype=float).ravel()
    if v.shape[0] != n:
        # Graceful fallback: strictly decreasing validities.
        v = np.linspace(0.95, 0.55, n)
    v = np.clip(v, 0.0, 1.0)

    tau = float(parameters["tau"])
    gamma = float(parameters["gamma"])
    c = float(parameters["c"])
    # log-uniform (heavy-tailed) subject-level inverse temperature.
    # Partially retreated to [0.25, 0.70] (beta in [1.8, 5.0], median ~3.0):
    # the iter-5 raise to [0.35, 0.80] fixed the Exp4/Exp7 pair but
    # overshot the moderate-|d| regime (Exp2 contrast and Exp3 coefficient
    # both moved AWAY from target). This is the midpoint between iter-3's
    # [0.15, 0.70] and iter-5's [0.35, 0.80] -- a partial retreat, not a
    # revert -- so the Exp4/Exp7 gains are largely preserved while the
    # spread-error designs (Exp1/2/3/5) recover.
    beta = 10.0 ** float(parameters["log10_beta"])
    eps = float(parameters["epsilon"])

    # (1) PARTIAL distrust inversion. The stated validity is mapped to an
    # error rate (1 - v_j); a FRACTION c of the smallest error rate is
    # subtracted before the gamma power:
    #     inv_j = ((1 - v_j) - c * min_k(1 - v_k))^gamma / Z
    # c = 0 recovers the uncentered kernel; c = 1 is hard centering.
    # c TRIMMED to [0.0, 0.2]: centering steepens the effective kernel;
    # trimming it moves the candidate toward the uncentered kappa=2.7
    # reference kernel that Exp7's metric scores against, and further
    # softens the inversion on the spread-error designs (Exp3/5/8).
    err = 1.0 - v
    centered = np.maximum(err - c * float(err.min()), 0.0)
    inv = np.power(centered, gamma)
    Z = float(inv.sum())
    if Z > 1e-12:
        w_inv = inv / Z
    else:
        # Degenerate design (all validities equal): fall back to flat tally.
        w_inv = np.full(n, 1.0 / n)

    # Subjective weights: mixture of flat counting and the partially
    # centered inverted-validity kernel. tau's lower bound SPLIT to 0.83
    # (midpoint of iter-3's 0.78 and iter-5's 0.88): the 0.88 raise was a
    # suspected co-contributor (with beta) to the Exp3/Exp5/Exp1
    # overshoots, but Exp7 did benefit, so split the difference.
    w = (1.0 - tau) / n + tau * w_inv

    # (2) Deterministic attention: every discriminating cue is always
